You play on a 15x12 grid viewed from above with the whole grid on screen and you must move to a bomb on screen to touch it and remove it. The bomb needs defusing within a time limit and if successful then depending on the level number, another one appears. As you move about the grid, any square you move from disappears so careful planning of your route must be made but if you do find yourself trapped then you can move the row your on, left or right.

There are two types of nasties on the screen and these are skull & crossbones or boots. The skulls stay where they are but move if the row they are on is being moved by you. The boots move around the grid themselves but cannot move onto blank squares. Flags can be collected for extra bonus points. If you touch a nasty, get trapped or fail to defuse a bomb within the time limit, then you lose on of five lives.

games.name: Captron
games.overview: In Captron you are a hunter for werewolves. From level to level you compose four nets from four parts each, dropping the parts to the bottom of playfield. To drop the part, you should pass over it, or drop another part on it. Werewolves are also in the playfield, and each contact with them means decrease of your lives. Dropping the part over the werewolf means his death and rebirth of another werewolf to kill you. To stop the werewolf you may set the dummy (blocker), which quantity is limited. Blockers appear on the playfield and may be collected. The quantity of werewolves, and the playfield shape's difficulty is increased with the level's number. The best scores are stored in high score table. Published in Software Club N°09.

games.name: Capture 2
games.overview: This is a game for one or two players. Pressing fire in port 2 will start Player VS Computer, while pressing fire in port 1 will start Player 1 VS Player 2. Take it in turn to capture a number of pieces. After one of you or the computer have reached the limited number of pieces to end the game, the player with the best score wins.

games.name: Capture (Courbois Software)
games.overview: Monsters have escaped from the zoo. It's your job to catch them. They are too dangerous to touch, so enclose them in fences. You do that by moving the walls to enclose them.

games.name: Capture (Future Publishing)
games.overview: Capture is a game of strategy and skill. Move your tiles around: preferably on to squares which are already occupied by your opponent. Published in Commodore Format 1995/07 (Issue #58).

games.name: Captured
games.overview: After your exploits in Soldier One, you now find yourself waking up in an unknown large building unaware how you got here. Finding a note in your pocket telling you to find parts of a code to exit from the building, you set off to explore the building and escape. Captured is a flick-screen platform game where you must navigate various platforms while avoiding obstacles and creatures. If you touch any creature then you lose one of five lives but you can jump and fall from any height. You are armed with a laser and a bomb but the laser can only be fired three times and you have one bomb. More lasers and bombs can be collected further into the game. Captured is a platform game for the Commodore 64 from 1986, developed by the first Scandinavian company developing games, Greve Graphics, and published by American Action. The main game was programmed by Bengt Caroli. The music and sound engine was programmed by Lars Hård. Lars also composed all original music and made all sound effects. The graphics were by Nils Hård.

games.name: Car Journey
games.overview: Can you run a successful trucking business? Call up the latest haulage contracts, select your vehicle and routes and go for the jobs which make the most money.  Watch out for the hazards and don't speed - the motorway police will catch you! You make the decisions and take the risks - to become a real truck driver you'll have to be calculating and sharp.

games.name: Car-O-Matic
games.overview: A logic brain game by Wojtek Wrona & Krysztof Matula with car pictures as the payoff. Another version of this game was distributed by Cybertech Laboratories with erotic images instead of cars as the payoff for logical triumph.

versions.label: Car O Matic (1996)(Eagleware International)[cr SCS TRC]
Car O Matic (1996)(Eagleware International)[cr LXT][t +2 LXT]

games.name: Car-Rac
games.overview: An avoid it game for one player by Trygve Gunderson that caused a bit of a flap at the time.

games.name: Car Race (F/S Soft)
games.overview: A single player, German language game, set on a racing track where the goal is to scoop up the pellets racing in one direction around the four-ringed track while avoiding cars racing around it in the opposite direction.

games.name: Car Race (Robtek)
games.overview: An educational game that teaches number recognition and teaches about places, like first through sixth, first place and last place in the race. Before and after and so forth. It simulates a race, then quizzes your child on who came in first, who came in last in the race. Who in before car number 3. Who came in after car number 1, etc.

games.name: Car Race (Tiger-Crew Disk PD)
games.overview: An over head racing game for one player from Michael Meiszl originally released in the German Tiger-Crew-Disk #028 (07/1996) and later in Courbois Software #6421 / a.k.a. "Auto Race". Both games are loosely based on an earlier PET game of some renowned.

games.name: Car Wars
games.overview:
An overhead racing game for 1-2 players developed by Fox/K Design using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.

It was released in 1989.

games.name: Carcrash (Markt & Technik)
games.overview: Do you feel called to be a Formula 1 driver and, you can save money! This game simulates the entire race on the C64: In his Carcrash game, the aim is to drive through a race track full of snakes as quickly as possible without damaging your car or anything else. If you manage to do this for 40 seconds (this time can be very long), you will get to the next level as a reward. Here, to your delight, the obstacles are much closer together. If you think you can leave the road and move better on the relatively flat green strip, you are mistaken: your car will leave the screen with a loud bang and the game will be over. Created by Sven Anlauf and published in 64'er 1992/10.

games.name: Card Land
games.overview: Another game for your brain, this time a card matching\memory game published in Commodore Scene #12 (10/1996). It also includes a Ping Pong game for a little more action. Really fantastic into screen with great graphics and sounds.

versions.label: Card Land (1995)(Nemesis Productions)[cr AVT][f NTSC PAL]

games.name: Card Sharks (ShareData)
games.overview: Based on a popular television show at the time it was released, Card Sharks is a question and answer guessing game in which you compete against a computer player or another "live person". Questions are asked based upon a poll of 100 people. You must guess how many out of 100 answered Yes or No. Your opponent then has the chance to guess whether the true answer is higher or lower than your answer. If you are right, you are taken to the "Cards" screen to play a video version of the "High Low" card game. Guessing correctly lets you keep control of the board, and the next question. If you lose, your opponent receives the next question. If you win enough times, you'll go to the "Big Bucks" card screen where you can bet all or part of your winnings on a more elaborate board of "High Low".

games.name: CardSwipe
games.overview: Roll dice to fill your four-part try with one of each card: Ace, King, Queen and Jack, if you can. A card game with dice from Payton Byrd.

games.name: Cargo
games.overview:
Cargo was a game which was being developed by Simon Nicol and Stavros Fasoulas under the Ducksoft Development label, and was meant for Silverbird Software. It apparently was to prove a point according to Said, that a budget title could be written overnight.   It had Simon’s star field in the background, and an Amidar style maze on the top.  There was to be a Vorpal loader and a cast off Hubbard track, but nothing seems to exist of this.  They may not have quite managed to get the tune included – unless a budding hacker can find it tucked away?

Richard Hewison of The Bird Sanctuary (a tribute site to Firebird and the other Telecomsoft labels) couldn’t recall the title, but suggested that at the time it would have likely gone on the Silverbird label. You can see elements of Quedex and Delta within the game, but also Simon’s distinctive star field.   It’s a neat puzzler where you colour in the maps in Painter style

games.name: Carnage
games.overview: In Carnage you race in a top-down view where every car goes with the same speed. And if you want to see the next track you must win your race; if you can't, unfortunately the game is over! In total there are 18 tracks. After every race you earn 800 pounds, and go to a shop where you can buy necessary things for your car like nitro and mines, or equipment for upgrade.

games.name: Carnival
games.overview:
Carnival is a pinball game for the Commodore 64 made with the Pinball Construction Kit.

It was developed by Bloodsong and released on PCS Club Disk #24 in 1991.

games.name: Carrier Command
games.overview: Carrier Command was one of the first real-time strategy games. You control an advanced cybernetic aircraft carrier complete with fighters, amphibious assault vehicles, laser defenses and a fleet of decoy drones. Your mission is to build a series of resource, factory, and defensive bases spanning an island chain. The only problem? At the other end of the chain is an even more advanced carrier under control of a terrorist organization with the same mission. As you move around the islands you must decide what facilities to build and where they will best support your advance. Resource islands provide materials that factory islands can use to build weapons and vehicles to replace your combat losses but both will be quickly overrun if the enemy attacks them while you are not present. You also have to ensure that your stockpiles of equipment are stored safely until you can find time to launch a resupply drone to bring them to your carrier. From your carrier, you can take first person control of your attack aircraft and amphibious tanks and use them to assault enemy islands or even the enemy carrier itself if you're lucky enough to find it. The weapon payloads on your vehicles are completely configurable based on your needs. An island invasion may require launching a virus bomb that will take over the enemy command systems or just blasting the base with a wire guided surface to surface missile. Ultimately, you have to find and destroy the enemy carrier but, doing so will require a solid supply infrastructure and a strategy for depriving your opponent of his.

games.name: Carrier Force
games.overview:
Carrier Force is an operational level game featuring combat between American and Japanese forces in 1942. The game was later updated as Carrier Strike. There are 4 scenarios covered in this game, Midway, Coral Sea, The Battle of the Eastern Solomons and The Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands. Every major warship and plane is accounted for and accurately detailed.

Each game turn represents one hour of action. The computer handles all the administrative chores while you give the orders and plot strategy. The game can be played by up to two people or in solitaire where the computer plays the Japanese. At the end of the game victory points are determined and the Japanese points are subtracted from the US points and compared to a table to determine the victory level. The game is advanced level and the playing time is 3 to 10 hours.

games.name: Carriers at War 1941-1945: Fleet Carrier Operations in the Pacific
games.overview: Carriers at War 1941-1945: Fleet Carrier Operations in the Pacific is a war simulation (wargame). In the game the player takes on the role of the task force commander in the pacific theater during World War II. In the six simulated conflicts the player can play as both the U.S. and the Japanese Empire. Included scenarios are Pearl Harbor, Coral Sea, Midway, Eastern Solomons, Santa Cruz and Philippine Sea. The game is played on a 72x84 hexagonal grid. The player can gives orders to the individual units and squadrons, which include naval vessels and land based aircraft. The computer then simulates how they perform their actions. The game is quasi real-time, meaning that the game can be paused at any given moment at which time the player can give orders to the units. All interaction with the game is through a menu interface. Orders that can be given to units include strike, escort, transport, support, refuel and more complex maneuvers such as strike routines.

games.name: Carrot Juggler
games.overview: Carrot Juggler is a 1-4 player pinball for the C64 using the C64 version of Olaf Lubeck's Pinball Construction Set. It was developed in 1991 by Ronald B. Rome. Released as part of Pcs Club Disk #27.

versions.label: Carrot Juggler(Ronald R.)[cr ASS][Created with PCS]

games.name: Carrun
games.overview: Carrun is a shmup inspired by Death Race 2000.

games.name: Carry on Laughing
games.overview: Carry on Laughing is a single screen platform game where you play the role of Mr Livewire whose job is to tidy up all the classrooms at St. Hexidecimals, a school for demented programmers. The school is made up of various screens and you must tidy up each screen by turning all the large X's into ticks while avoiding the various people, creatures and objects that move around the screen. At the bottom of the screen is a bar with Mr Livewire walking from left to right across with X's on it, and a screen is completed when all the X's are ticks and Mr Livewire reaches the right of the bar. On the walls surrounding each classroom are an arrow and you can select which classroom to go to next with a small grid on the bottom left showing where you have visited. As well as platforms to walk on there are various ways to move up to higher levels like ladders, bars and on one screen you can use bubbles to float upwards. If you are touched by the people, creatures or objects then you lose one of three lives and all the ticks have turned into X's. Two players can play with each player taking it in turns when the other player loses a life.

games.name: Cartels & Cutthroat$
games.overview: Cartels & Cutthroat$ is notable for being one of the first business sims in existence. 1-8 players compete for profit in this simulation of cut-throat competition that is a simulatio of the basic tenets in finance and economics. Understanding these concepts is key to winning the game, which involving setting your production level and price where marginal costs equal marginal revenues, borrow funds when prime rates are low to expand, and minimize cost per unit. You must also pay careful attention to the state of the economy and consumers' tastes, both of which change constantly. If you're unsure of what to do, your advisor in the game will guide you in the right direction.

games.name: Carvalho: Los Pájaros de Bangkok
games.overview: The story begins on any day and in a city that is not appropriate to name, when the detective -in this case you- Pepe Carvalho receives from Bangkok a mysterious call from an old friend, Teresa Marsé, who very scared requires your help: - "It's a miracle I can call you, I'm in a hurry, they want to kill us, Pepe ..." - Kill yourself? To who? To the whole expedition? The white race? The Catalans? - Archit and me. - Who is Archit? - "It's too long to tell and I'm not sure here, it's my companion, they're chasing us, Pepe, I'm serious, do something, come on, Pepe!" With just this information and suffering all kinds of hardships , you meet her family (her son, a waiter, her husband, a dog-sitter, and her father, an old, stingy, millionaire who wants nothing to do with her) at the travel agency that took her to Bangkok, where her guide She informs everyone of what happened: "In Bangkok, Teresa meets a young native -Archit- who falls in love, but he turns out to be a diamond dealer." Teresa can not think of anything else to convince him to steal diamonds from her. boss, Jungle Kid, but his son discovers them, and Archit has no choice but to kill him ... Now the whole Thai mafia is chasing them, and it will be difficult for them to escape ... "With all this, nobody seems to want to go looking Teresa or hire someone for the trip. You get to convince your father that something has to be done, and he chooses you as a forced volunteer after haggling the price of the trip with the owner of the agency. It also refuses to give you more than 200,000 baths for the trip ... ... After a long plane ride you arrive in Bangkok, and you do not know where to start looking. You only know that you have to go to the Spanish embassy in Bangkok, where the ambassador will explain your mission more thoroughly.

versions.label: Carvalho Los Pajaros De Bangkok(Dinamic Software)(es)[cr Blasters]

games.name: Cascade
games.overview: A puzzle game published in Visionparty 2002, in GO64! 2002/12, and in Loadstar #232. Your task is to pop as many bubbles as you can. At least 2 neighboring bubbles of the same color are needed for this. The more bubbles you can destroy at once the more points you will get. If all the bubbles are destroyed you will get 500 extra points. Have much fun!

games.name: Cashman
games.overview: Released in Game On 1994/03 this platform shooter by Electric Boys Entertainment Software (EBES) has you shooting familiar enemies to pick up coins. Get enough coins and you can move on to the next level, where you repeat the process.

games.name: Casino Blackjack (Dragon Magic Software)
games.overview: A blackjack game created by Eric J. Floehr & Ollie Floehr for Dragon Magic Software.

games.name: Casino Blackjack (Softdisk Publishing)
games.overview: A 1993 computerized Blackjack game for up to 7 players for the Commodore 64. It was developed by John M. Campbell and published in Loadstar #107.

games.name: Casino Craps
games.overview: Casino Craps is a dice game in which the players make wagers on the outcome of the roll, or a series of rolls, of a pair of dice. Players may wager money against a bank. This was developed by Dave Pedri and published by Casino Software in 1986.

games.name: Casino Poker
games.overview:
A single-player, casino game for one created by Comp-U-Soft and released in 1993. There are 2 types of games included. In Casino Poker, you play a slot machine version of 5 Card Draw. You start off with 20 pints and lose or win points depending on your final hand. However after playing 15 hands it will get a bit harder and you'll need at least a pair of Jacks to win.   
 
In Draw Poker this is a one on one contest between you and the dealer. You can Call, Raise, Fold or Pass, but so can they. To reset discards push F1.

games.name: Casino Simulator
games.overview: Casino Simulator is a Las Vegas style roulette game for up to eight players. Every player starts with 5000 on hand and the game ends when the last human player runs out of cash. The main game screen consists of the standard standard Las Vegas roulette betting table. When all the bets have been placed and the option "Spin Wheel" is selected an animation of a spinning roulette wheel is displayed and then the results shows up. After that the table has to be cleared before new bets can be placed. The players can view wheel and player statistics any time during the betting phase.

games.name: Castalia
games.overview:
Mordred, an evil wizard, has stolen the Great Cup of Caslalia, plunging all the land into darkness. You have learned that the cup is hidden in a great underground castle. To recover the cup, you must make your way through many caves and caverns leading to the castle. The journey will be difficult; the caves are filled with goblins and traps. Can you return the cup and restore order to the world? 
 
Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1991/05, which was an insert in the standard Compute! magazine at the time.

games.name: Castle Adventure
games.overview: Sneak into the castle and find the treasure. Beware of guards, bats and the Baron.

games.name: Castle Blackstar
games.overview: Castle Blackstar is a single player text adventure set in a world of magic. The player takes the role of an adventurer who has been dispatched by Lady Artemis into Castle Blackstar to recover an artifact, an orb. Any 'mortal treasure' recovered can be kept. Progress through the game is recorded by points the player accumulates in their travels.

games.name: Castle Dracula
games.overview: Your quest is to find and enter Count Dracula's castle, find the Count himself before killing him with a stake. As you explore the castle, as well as items to help you, you will find various creatures like ghouls and zombies which can be avoided or killed. A certain ghoul has to be killed as it will attempt to take any item you have on your person. Any items taken can be found in a vast cavern. Castle Dracula is a text adventure where text appears on the screen describing your location and you type in commands with the keyboard to interact with your surroundings.

games.name: Castle Dungeon
games.overview: A maze is quickly shown to you and then the fog of war sets in and you can only see the section of the map around you. How quickly can you get to the exit of the labyrinth and free yourself. Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/06 (Issue #12), and Stonysoft #1912. Published in English and Dutch.

games.name: Castle Dungeon Adventure
games.overview: Published in micro Adventurer 1984/07 (Issue #09). A text adventure with 50,000 possible locations, so make sure you don't get lost. You have to make your way to the bottom of an old dungeon where you'll find a key to open all the gold-filled chests. beware of pits and creatures in the dungeon.

games.name: Castle Hassle
games.overview:
Castle Hassle (Mystic Mansion in Europe) is a puzzle game for the 8-bit Atari and Commodore 64 computers.

Played from a top-down perspective, the player controls a small ghost within a haunted mansion, who is tasked with collecting a number of treasures. The ghost is armed with a small gun, which can fire in the 4 cardinal directions, and can be used to defeat monsters and solve puzzles. Each room has a short description which might provide a hint, and the player has a limited timeframe to gather the treasure on each level. The player starts with 10 lives, and if all are lost it's game over. Contains 3 difficulty levels: child, teenager, and adult, which influence the time available each level.

games.name: Castle-Kingdom
games.overview: Castle-Kingdom is a game that borrows heavily from the old Atari Arcade game Crystal Castles. It was released to the public domain in 1985.

games.name: Castle Master
games.overview:
Castle Master is the fourth and final individual game to use the Freescape first-person solid 3D game system (after Driller, Dark Side and Total Eclipse). As a Prince or Princess armed with a slingshot, you have to explore a medieval castle to free your beloved from the evil Magister. 

Gameplay combines action and puzzle-solving, across four primary towers with three levels each. Doors must be opened using one of the ten included keys. These are unmarked, as are the various potions - making it a challenge to know which keys open which doors, and which potions are beneficial. 

Contact with ghouls drains your energy, as does falling too far (there are narrow pathways to negotiate), while eating cheese can replenish this. Movement and aiming are controlled separately.

games.name: Castle Master II: The Crypt
games.overview:
Castle Master II: The Crypt is an Action Adventure game, developed by Incentive Software Ltd and published by Domark Software Ltd, which was released in Europe in 1991.

Set in and around a dark and eerie castle, cross a shark-infested moat and risk life and limb in a desperate rescue bid. Choose to free either the Prince or Princess. Battle with the evil spirits using just your slingshot. Search for keys, potions and clues to unravel the mysteries of "Castle Eternity". Use your eyes and ears to discover solutions to the brain-twisting puzzles. Secret rooms, dark corridors and hidden traps, all in superb solid 3D makes Castle Master a unique and atmospheric action adventure experience. Enter "Castle Eternity" if you dare! You could be there forever.

As with other platform releases, the Amiga version of Castle Master II: The Crypt was only released as part of a compilation, no standalone retail release exists.

Castle Master II The Crypt (1990)(Domark)[cr Nato]
Castle Master II The Crypt (1990)(Domark)[cr Action]
Castle Master II The Crypt (1990)(Domark)[cr Cyberpunx]
Castle Master II The Crypt (1990)(Domark)[cr Bonzai]

games.name: Castle Maze Adventure
games.overview: Collect any valuables you find inside a castle. Simple text-adventure. You are in a forest. Your mission is to explore your surroundings and collect any valuables you find. Your journey will take you to an old castle, full of twisting and turning corridors, horrible sorcerers, and mysterious spiders. Will you unravel all the secrets of the castle, collect all the treasure, and escape alive?

versions.label: Castle Maze Adventure(The Guild Adventure Software)

games.name: Castle Nightmare
games.overview: In an old chest is a rough, precious diamond. Join Simon, the hero of Castle Nightmare, through 10 levels. Open the chest, grab the diamond, and free Simon from the prison. But it is a long and dangerous way to freedom. You can find the key of every room and put it in the closing hole that appears on it. A secret opens and you step into an even scarier room. Beware of the hangman who guards the key, bats who yearn for your life, ghosts that block your way! Use your intellect, so that you choose the right course and do not run against an invisible wall button on the lamp that lights you the way out of the dark room Huge monsters, of which you only see the eyes, threaten you. And hurry, because time is running away ...

games.name: Castle Northstar
games.overview:
A text adventure game published as a type-in game in the book "Castles & Kingdoms". 

The sword Deathtouch was alive. It sensed the darkness and the coolness of the stone. It was self-aware and in that awareness lay a sense of duty. The sword Deathtouch was Chaos incarnate. True to its name, no living creature could survive after being dealt a wound from its edge or point. The sword Deathtouch was a prisoner in the Realm of the Dead, a fitting place for it. For what death could it deal to those beyond life? What torture could it inflict on those tortured beyond the grave? The sword Deathtouch had not tasted warm blood for a long time. Butwarm bloods were crossing the river. Soon the blade of Chaos would be among the living, and many would die. The Priests of the Snake were nervous, as they had cause to be in this creepy sub-dungeon of Castle Northstar. And the High Priest, though outwardly confident, quivered in his robes at the misty waters of the river Styx. This was a spellbound place, the only place in the kingdom where the living joined the dead. The ferryman was Death' s minion; and the Ruler of the Dead was a shade of evil-a shadow of Alabastria, the Black Kingdom beyond the doors of Star gate. He held the keys to unlocking the Demons of Chaos and, by the tongue of the Snake, those keys would ride the ferry in the pocket of a red cloak. The girl was Human. She was too young to have reason for fright. The tall Priest spoke kindly to her and allowed no one near her but the two young guards. They never spoke at all. The Pries t had given her a bracelet and promised her another if she was good. She missed her father but she did not cry. She'd seen many wonders on her journey and had not had time to think of her family. She couldn't see much here because of the fog. She could hear strange sounds though, moaning in pain, softly whispering in agony through the mist. She was now a little frightened and moved closer to the High Priest, her protector. She wanted to cry but she could not. She could feel the tears within her but she could not cry. So the mist and the unseen voices cried for her, as though they knew her fate. The ferry cut through the dark water and through the hovering mist, bumped into the shore and grounded. The Priests and the girl disembarked and moved away from the shore. The ferry backed away and turned into the mists, the single oar of the ferryman rippling the water very slightly. The ferry moved across the river as if its pilot could see through the mists. Maybe he could. It stopped on the opposite shore and awaited its next passenger. The sword Deathtouch could sense the approaching Priests, warm bloods all. A deal had been struck that would return it to the upper world. Soon it would drink deep draughts and Law would be no more. The Master of the Dead would have the girl. She would serve him and remind him of beauty in a realm of zombies and shades. Beauty was his weakness, his perversion. It had cost him his Alabastrian citizenship. He'd been expelled for being less than perfectly evil. But he'd have the girl. She would comfort him with her presence, yet torture him at the same time. For he could not touch her and she could not lay eyes on him. Even in the Land of the Dead, Law protects innocence. He did not wish a confrontation with the Law. In such a case even Deathtouch would not protect him. Besides, that sword was going into sunlight. A fine trade, was it not? In the upper reaches of Northstar, a hero began his descent. He was canny and bold. But Northstar was a harsh obstacle, its traps cruel and deadly. The vermin of the upper levels hungered for the remains of the would-be heroes. Above Northstar, the sky was as blue as ever, shading the valley lake and contrasting the greens, greys and snowcap whites of the surrounding countryside. A hawk soared, a drama played, a hero strove, a menace rose and in the end five Priests were slain and Deathtouch drank hero's blood. The Master of the Dead was sa

games.name: Castle of Doom
games.overview:
Released in the book "Commodore 64 Games Book" and also in C+VG 1984/06 (Issue #32). Explore the rooms within the castle walls, look for treasure and try to avoid the slime monsters and killer robots. Points are gained by moving over question marks and killing monsters or robots with your Proton gun. As you move off the screen from one room you are presented with another. Move back and you return to the same room but now with 
different contents! You are killed if you touch the electrified walls or any of the monsters. Some monsters are faster than others and the robots are very dangerous.

games.name: Castle of Dracula
games.overview: Escape with your life from the Castle of Dracula in this 1983 text adventure developed by Jaan Jiri Kiraly.

versions.label: Castle of Dracula (1983)(The Guild Adventure Software)

games.name: Castle of Spirits
games.overview:
Castle of Spirits is a 1988 text adventure by Anthony Maro for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Anthony Maro and published in the following:

•   Loadstar #056
•   Digital Talk #003 (26.09.1993)

A text adventure intended to help you learn techniques you can use in your own programs. The Castle of Spirits is a small interactive adventure game which has most of the features you're accustomed to in text games. You use verb-noun commands like "Go House" or "Take Box". If you want to take a two-word noun, such as an oil can take the second word, eg. "Take Can".  Normal shorthand such as N, S, E, W for the cardinal directions, U and D can be used for up and down.  
 
You are in a large courtyard with a dilapidated shed in the corner. The south edge is lined by an old stone wall with a portcullis in the middle. Whilst going about your business a more than slightly deranged apparition appears. He seems to be creaming some nonsense about no escape. The ghost very impolitely laughs in your face and then vanishes to whatever unsightly place he appeared from. You will need to prepare to take on all the horrors a gothic castle can dish out and if you are lucky, you may get out of this castle alive!

games.name: Castle of Terror (CP Verlag)
games.overview:
Short horror-themed platformer released in 1988.

"You were caught in the "Castle of Terror". Try to find the exit by moving through each lineup to the next. This begins after you have reached the top of the screen.

That sounds easy, but numerous ghosts, demons and other beings are not exactly helpful in finding the exit. As a little tip, we can tell you that the best thing to do is to avoid everything that moves." Published in Magic Disk 64 1988/11.

The game was followed by a sequel, Die Pyramide in 1989.

games.name: Castle of Terror (Melbourne House)
games.overview: In this graphic adventure game from Melbourne House, the player must venture into the vampire's castle to rescue a fair maid. Players proceed through the game by reading a description of each scene, then entering one- or two word commands at a prompt. The commands can be simple or complex, and the player can perform more than one action on a single line. Animated characters feature in some scenes of the game, and there is background music during play.

versions.label: Castle of Terror (1985)(Melbourne House)[cr Strike Force Movers Mayhem]
notes: Cracked by Strike Force Movers Mayhem

games.name: Castle Quest
games.overview:
Very tough avoid-the-walls game in which you must guide your lander to the crystals on each screen. Holding down the fire button thrusts, just don't thrust too far!

Released by Commodore User 1986/08 and created by Sandy Munro.

games.name: Castle Raid!
games.overview:
An action game by Paul Klemond and published in 1983.  Defend the castle from the fierce raiders. The objective is to hurl rocks at guys trying to get in your castle. At the end of each stage, you are awarded a shield. At the end of the seventh stage, you are greeted by a princess.

Possibly the first C64 game to feature speech, although it slows down things considerably.

games.name: Castle Warlock
games.overview: This is an interesting game, though it suffers from "guess the verb" syndrome. It also has a spelling error such that if you type what you are told to type, you can't proceed. But now that I've planted that seed in your head you can probably figure it out and open the way to your own personal red carpet when you defeat the Warlock and escape his stronghold.

games.name: Castle Wolfenstein
games.overview:
In this game, the player takes control of a lone prisoner who has been taking captive in a large castle occupied by the Nazis. Getting out of the cell and picking up a weapon is just the beginning; the ultimate goal is to acquire the war plans of the Nazis, and escape from Castle Wolfenstein alive.

Castle Wolfenstein is notable for being the first game that incorporated stealth-based gameplay mechanics. The player navigates the hero through the top-down corridors and rooms of the castle. The main gameplay challenge lies in dealing with the guards who patrol the castle and will be alerted to any noise made by the player. It is possible to shoot the guards, but the ammunition in the game is scarce, and some guards are very hard to kill, so the preferred course of action is moving without being noticed. If the player surprises a guard with a gun drawn, the guard will surrender, and the player will be able to frisk him for valuable items.

The player should also search the treasure chests scattered across the castle. Some of them contain war plans, which are essential for winning the game; others have useful items, such as bullets, grenades, bulletproof vests, and guard uniforms. The uniforms can be worn for disguise; however, higher-ranked SS guards will be able to recognize the intruder. Chests might also contain food and beverage; imbibing alcohol will result in a temporary loss of aim and balance for the player character.

The game's sound effects include some of the earliest examples of digital voice samples. The guards would sometimes shout out short phrases in German in an attempt to stop the protagonist.

games.name: Castles and Creatures
games.overview: Castles and Creatures is a Dungeons and Dragons inspired RPG developed by Stephen Henwood and published by NET Software in 1983.

games.name: Castlevania
games.overview: Every hundred years, the dark vampire known as Dracula resurrects and terrorizes the land. A vampire hunter named Simon Belmont bravely ventures into the Count's mansion in order to defeat him. Along the way he'll have to defeat skeletons, bats, fishmen, medusa heads and other evil creatures. Castlevania is a side-scrolling platform action game. The player takes the role of Simon Belmont, who is able to jump and crack his whip directly in front of him. Power-ups can be obtained by defeating enemies or by whipping candles that appear in the castle. One such power-up increases the power and length of Simon's whip. Different weapons can be gathered which consume hearts when used, these hearts can also be collected from monsters and candles. Additionally, some walls will hide secrets such as the health-restorative turkey or the Double and Triple shot abilities for the weapons Simon has collected. At the end of each section of the castle is a boss, which must be defeated. Progression through the castle eventually leads to a confrontation with Count Dracula himself.

games.name: Castor
games.overview: A puzzle game similar to Columns that was published in the German magazine Game On in their 1995/03 issue. Castor is a falling block puzzle game similar to Columns. Stones consisting of three blocks of varying colors drop down and have to be arranged in the right way. Pressing the fire-button will rearrange the blocks that make up a stone. At least four blocks of the same color have to be lined up vertically, horizontally or diagonally in order to clear them. The more stones are cleared at once, the higher the score. A level ends after a set number of stones (which increases with every level) has been dropped. Every 10,000 points the speed of the stones increases. If the stones reach the top of the screen, the game ends.

games.name: Cat & Rat
games.overview: A collect-em-up game created by Johan Persson and released in GO64! 2002/07 (preview version). In the game you control a rat, you want to eat the cheese while avoiding the poison and the cat. Brutus the dog can help keep the cat away, but is very sleepy. Time to eat cheese!

games.name: Cataclysm
games.overview: Cataclysm is pure shoot-em-up action. The lunar city of Erriam is under fearsome bombardment from the saucers fo the Jovian empire. You are the commander of the lone laser outpost, and your mission is-hold out as long as you can, or there can only be one outcome - CATACLYSM!

games.name: Catacombs (Anirog Software)
games.overview: Your village is cursed with a plague and the only solution available is for you to go into the underground Catacombs to find a mysterious sorcerer. No one is sure if he is good or evil but his powers came from potions he brewed so you need to get the formula for the potion needed and collect the ingredients. Before you start your quest you can choose which role to take, fighter Duke or cunning Witch, each with their own strength and weaknesses. As you explore, you will encounter creatures that can be talked to or some will need fighting and killed before you are killed. The game is a graphic text adventure with text on the screen describing each location you are in and a picture of what you can see. You type in commands with the keyboard to interact with your surroundings.

games.name: Catacombs (Ion Intenational)
games.overview:
Published in Ahoy! magazine 1987/01 (Issue #37), and also in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1994/11. This is a rogue-like dungeon crawler. Being the ardent treasure hunter that you are, you had a hard time resisting the stories about the Catacombs of Darkness and the fantastic caches of gold hidden there by the mysterious builders of the underground fortress. 

Armed with only a torch, you descended the steps leading down to the catacombs without hesitating, ignoring the weird cries emanating from the dimly lit crypt, images of bulging chests of ill-gotten lucre swimming in your mind. Your purpose on each level is to avoid the traps and monsters, get as many gold chests as possible, and find the key that unlocks the door leading to the next level. 

On the first five levels, this is relatively easy, since the catacombs are illuminated. But on the next five levels, the lights arc out, and the only things you can see are the objects which arc within range of your torch. It takes an extensive search, as well as caution, to avoid the traps and monsters while you look. 

There are five types of critters living in the catacombs: skulls, wizards, bats, spirits, and snakes. There are three of these guardians on each level, and they are quite intelligent and relentless in their efforts to catch you. If one of the monsters catches you, the game ends.

games.name: Catacombs of Gold
games.overview: Catacombs of Gold is a single player fantasy role-play video game. Journey into the dark and dangerous world beneath the castle fo Count Damion. But take some advice to make your journey a little safer and perhaps a little more profitable. You'll begin this journey with three hearts, 100 units of speed, strength and morale. If any of these four drop to zero you will remain in the catacombs forever. All you take with you is an old and unreliable magic ring. It was given to you by the only mane to ever enter the catacombs and return safely to the outside world. He warned you about the snakes and bats, that won't hurt you, but they do steal weapons and supplies. other monsters like the undead are under the Vampire's control and will try to hurt you, if you give them a chance. Other chambers will fill with deadly gas, you can try to outrun it or try to use the ring. The ring will also create a trapdoor to the next level which you can use to descend even deeper. Be sure to have something to make a map with, because you'll need it!

games.name: Catalypse
games.overview: Catalypse is a horizontally-scrolling shoot'em up where you guide your ship against the alien CLIO civilization through five big levels, including a moon base, an alien forest, dark caverns, and an ancient city. The levels are full of small enemies, both stationary and mobile. There are also bigger mid-level creatures and of course level end guardians. These include screen-filling giant creatures, robots and spaceships. On your way you can collect cumulative weapon power ups hidden in capsules. Available are angled forward shots, a backward shot, an angled bouncing laser, a powerful forward laser, and up to two hovering and indestructible satellites. Unique characteristics of the game include sampled speech in the introduction and an extended animated ending sequence.

games.name: Catastrophe
games.overview: Catastrophe (Catastrophes in Europe) is a single screen building game where you must carry bricks with a helicopter one at a time from a barge and place them on an island to build a hotel as high as you can. You must try to get the highest score you can over six days and each day is shown by the sun moving from east to west across the top of the screen. Every time you place a new storey then you receive a point and as you build you are competing against the computer or a second player who are building at the same time. As each day progresses there are a couple of natural disasters that occur with the first two being a flood and an earthquake which removes bricks for a short space of time. As the days progress then storm winds and lightning can also occur and a plane keeps flying across the screen, and if touched carrying a brick then you lose the brick. The game is over once the six days are over but even if you can't build anymore on an earlier day the game keeps playing. If you leave the joystick alone then after a certain time the computer takes over but you receive no score.

games.name: Catch a Byte to Eat
games.overview: Catch a Byte to Eat is a simple Snake game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Bruce Beck. The year of release is not currently known.

versions.label: Catch a Byte to Eat(Bruce Beck)

games.name: Catch a Thief
games.overview: You are the Directory of Security in a world famous Museum of Fine Arts. Since the museum is being renovated, it is particularly vulnerable to burglars specializing in theft of rare and precious objects. The museum comprises 3 levels, 81 rooms, 6 corridors and 4 elevators. The building complex can be viewed through any of the three monitors in your office, using the 91 cameras installed throughout the complex. Your salary depends on your success at preventing the theft of the museums's priceless treasures. Varying salary levels increase the difficulty of your task. You direct the staff of security guards and give them tasks to catch the thief or thieves.

versions.label: Catch a Thief (1987)(Tri Micro)[cr ESI Starline]
Catch a Thief (1987)(Tri Micro)[cr ESI Danish Gold]

games.name: Catch-a-Trooper
games.overview: Survival! Fight between land, sky and sea with Catch-a-Trooper. You will experience at home, all the charm of a real training with various difficult tests of skill, courage and endurance. So if you feel ready to be the solitary hero of an unbelievable, committed and active adventure start now. During the game throw the nets to survive. If you make it long enough you will have managed to take a well-deserved rest in the beautiful islands of a remote atoll in the Pacific. Relax and calm down, you are on board a small boat in the hope of catching the biggest of fish, falling from the sky. Then move on to take out the advancing soldiers. Help soldiers who fall from the transport helicopter avoid the voracious shark and flying birds of prey.

games.name: Catch (Exclusive Designs)
games.overview: Catch is an action game created by Eddy Scholten and Martin Hoekstra and released in 1992. Move your block with the joystick in port#2 and catch all the falling objects. Fire button will speed up your block.

games.name: Catch II
games.overview: The sky is falling! Well, at least all the aliens, planets, spaceships and monoliths are, and they are all falling at different rates and trajectories. And like the man says, you gotta catch 'em all. Miss 3 and you'll be starting over.

games.name: Catch It
games.overview:
A 2-player only dueling game released in Happy Computer 1989/03 and also in 64'er Sonderheft 61. Catch it challenges you! Defend yourself against satellites! Defend your skin - in an arena of the future. The satellites and the enemy's projectiles make your life difficult. The aim of this game is to snatch flying objects from under your opponent's nose. These are deployed by a blue satellite on its orbit, which occasionally provides supplies. The first to collect 20 of these objects wins. All objects are picked up by touching them. If a projectile hits you, it means the loss of one energy unit. The laws of acceleration will throw you off the trajectory and sometimes reverse the controls for a while. 

When a player has used up all seven vital energy units, his symbol disappears and he has to wait briefly for his next spaceship. If all seven missiles are used up, the game is lost. All the while you should watch out for the satellites whizzing around, as each collision costs one aircraft. A well-aimed shot will knock them out for a short time and give you a point as a bonus. But be careful - after the new release, the satellites will initially be bulletproof!
The game also has a small surprise in store for particularly goal-oriented joystick acrobats. But you have to find out for yourself.

games.name: Catch the Bouncing Ball
games.overview:
In this game you have to well, catch a little white bouncing ball. You control a tire or donut shaped sprite. The goal is to catch the ball directly in the center of the player sprite by pressing the fire button. You cannot move while the fire button is pressed down.

This game was developed by Tobias Gohlke (also known as Toggle) for the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 2006 (C64CGC).

games.name: Catch Them Up!
games.overview: Originally released as part of the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 2004 (C64CGC). This one fits the bill.

games.name: Cats and Mice
games.overview: In this game created by Maurie Yanney and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1993/01, you're a mouse in this  fast-paced one player game and you must maneuver through various mazes to reach a number of cheeses. To add a little excitement to the game, the cheeses also move! And to dial things up even further, several cats are chasing you! the object of the tame is simple to each all the cheese while avoiding the cats.

games.name: Cats 'n' Dogs
games.overview:
Cats 'n' Dogs is a 1-2 player puzzle/board game for the Commodore 64. The game is essentially a take on Tic-Tac-Tie/Nought and Crosses, except instead of X's and O's, you have...well cats and dogs. There is also another difference between this and standard Tic-Tac-Toe, and that you must get 4 in a row instead of 3. So it's basically a cross between Tic-Tac-Toe, and Connect 4.

The game was developed by Fred Karg and Included in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988/01 (Issue #55).

games.name: Cauldron
games.overview: Playing a witch, you must assemble the six ingredients required to kill off your arch-rival, an evil pumpkin. The ingredients are all located in underground buildings, each of which can only be entered once you've found the appropriate key. The keys are located overground, and you must fly around on your broom to collect them. The overground sections play like standard shoot 'em ups, as your broom is not affected by gravity and can fire bullets using your magic energy. Bats, fireballs and even seagulls are among the many creatures trying to stop you - contact will cost you more energy than shooting at them would. There are energy recharges on offer. Once you go underground, the gameplay becomes a test of precision platform jumping, including some Manic Miner-esque blind jumps. The six underground sections can be completed in a variety of orders, but you will sometimes reach points that can't be completed without objects from other sections, so a lot of back-tracking is required. Although you start with nine lives, they won't last all that long at first.

games.name: Cauldron II: The Pumpkin Strikes Back
alt_names: Hexenküche II: Der Kürbis schlägt zurück
Hexenkueche II: Der Kuerbis Schlaegt Zurueck
games.overview: An evil witch has brought evil and darkness to the enchanted wood, wiping out all but 1 of the innocent pumpkins. As the poem in the instructions sheet explains, the only way to put things right is to capture a lock of her hair, then take it to the cauldron and cast a spell to undo things. Controlling the pumpkin is difficult at first, as it has a very high bounce, the exact level of which can be toggled using the 5 key. Direction can only be changed when the ball is on the ground. Ricocheting into enemies costs energy, and you only gain weaponry by landing into magic pools. The starting positions are random, making mapping advisable and increasing the initial challenge. Even then, enemies respawn quickly, so all you're doing is buying a little time to pass them. Others can't be shot, and must be passed by possessing the right object - possibly one of the 5 you will ultimately need to vanquish the witch.

versions.label: Cauldron II The Pumpkin Strikes Back (1986)(Palace Software)
Cauldron 2 The Pumpkin Strikes Back (1986)(Palace)[cr Computerbrain Cracking Service]

Cauldron II The Pumpkin Strikes Back (1986)(Palace Software)[cr REM][t +5 REM][Docs][#173]

games.name: Cave Climber
games.overview:
This tough little platformer is a German language clone of the 1983 Konami arcade game Roc 'N Rope. It was developed by Thorsten Lange and published by Verlag Heinz Heise GmbH in Input 64 1985/09.

An English translation under the name Rock 'N Rope name was completed but never officially published.

games.name: Cave Explorer
games.overview: A crystal caverns type underground text adventure game, find the 7 treasures and make your way back to the surface.

games.name: Cave Fighter
games.overview: Cave Fighter is a platform game where you have to move from left to right with the screen scrolling when you move to escape various caves before a timer runs out. You can walk left or right but to jump you have to hold the fire button down, a gauge increases and the longer you hold it the higher and further you will jump. Careful use of this is needed as you can only land on the ground or the top of a platform, if you touch the sides of a platform, wall or touch an obstacle like water or spikes then you lose a life. As you get deeper into a cave you will encounter various creatures but you have a gun that fires in multiple directions and will kill any creature with some taking various amounts of shots to remove. If you touch a creature then you lose a life as well. Ropes can be used to climb and to get across gaps between platforms. Before you start the game you can select the level number (1-31) and how many lives (1-99).

games.name: Cave Girl Clair
games.overview:
Cave Girl Clair is an educational adventure game.

Resourceful and handy, Clair must survive the challenges of the New Stone Age. When her people migrate to their summer cave, Clair and her pet rabbit are mistakenly left behind. But she is a spunky girl and knows they will return one day.

The player starts at their cave, where they must decide from two difficulty levels. At the cave, the player must decide whether they they will start their fire with flint or with a stick. The player must explore a number of screens, in which Clair must gather food, firewood, and medicinal herbs, as well as construct tools. The player defend themselves from dangerous creatures. The goal is to survive four seasons until Clair's family returns to her cave.

games.name: Cave-Guennie
games.overview: A Boulder-Dash style game published in Game On 1989/05 and in GO64! 2005/11 / a.k.a. "Caveman".

versions.label: Cave Guennie (1989)(CP Verlag Game On)[cr Hotline Fun]
Cave Guennie (1989)(CP Verlag Game On)[cr Hotline]
Cave Guennie (1989)(CP Verlag Game On)[cr Dualis]
Cave Guennie (1989)(CP Verlag Game On)[cr Zeroboys]
Cave Guennie (1989)(CP Verlag Game On)[cr Weird Science]
Cave Guennie (1989)(CP Verlag Game On)[cr Vision]

games.name: Cave Kooks
games.overview: Inspired by the arcade game Dig Dug, Cave Kooks is a single screen game viewed from the side where you have to dig through the dirt to remove creatures over various levels. The creatures in question are threatening to collapse the Earth's crust as they burrow to make their habitats and you must stop them. You must reach each of the creatures which vary in numbers the further you progress and shoot out a bar and when it hits a creature you can spin them to remove them. Some of the creatures fire at you while others move from one tunnel to another. On later levels more creatures appear on the surface and these have to be removed as well. if you touch any creature or it's bullets then you lose one of three lives and the level has to be started again.

games.name: Cave of Death
games.overview: Released in 64'er Sonderheft 49 in 1989. A secret mission takes you to the underground caves of death. Try to avoid the myriad dangers and reach the rescue base. An uninhabited planet, its surface thick with impenetrable clouds of poison gas, but mineral resources under ground could not be ignored. The planet, named Acorn could be mined and the caves used for habitation. But when attackers came, they turned the defenses back towards us and now the only hope the hostages have is if we can penetrate the alien-upgraded defenses and save our people!

games.name: Cave of the Ice Ape
games.overview:
Your search was finally over.... 
A few months ago, your true love, Maxine, left on an expedition to the Himalaya mountains. She was not heard from again. You have searched for her ever since. One day, with the snow blowing and the temperature below zero, you heard a scream coming from a cave. You looked inside the cave to find Maxine-held prisoner by a large apelike creature. 

Cave of the Ice Ape is a game for the C-64 which features music, sound effects, and sprite animation. Using a joystick in Port 1, your goal is to rescue Maxine as many times as you can without being hit by one of the snowballs that the Ice Ape losses down at you. In order to free Maxine, you will need three sticks of TNT. These will appear throughout the cave. Do not run into any portion of the cave, or you will blow up and lose one of the four lives you began the game with (after all, you are carrying TNT). You have only 40 seconds to collect the three sticks of TNT. If you do not collect them within the set time, you lose a life. If you do get the TNT, Maxine shows her appreciation and you receive HX points. Another rescue attempt follows, only this time the snowballs move a little faster. After each successful rescue, the snowballs pick up speed. Released in Ahoy! 1987/06 (Issue #42).

versions.label: Cave of the Ice Ape (1987)(Ahoy! Ion International)

games.name: Cave of the Reaper
games.overview: Cave of the Reaper is a 1987 text adventure for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Steve Shelton and published in Loadstar #035.

games.name: Cave-Quest
games.overview: A simple but nice exploration game created by Douglas Hoch & Marc Gallo and published by Mystic Software, in 1989, but also re-released by them in 1990.

games.name: Cave Quest
games.overview: Magazine: Epic 3000 n 7

games.name: Cavelon
games.overview: The princess is being held captive inside the castle, and it's up to you (the knight) to rescue her. In order to do this, though, you need to collect the door pieces that are scattered in the six dungeons that await you, and defeat the black wizard in the end. Time is against you, so you need to hurry up. Once you have collected all pieces, the exit door will open, and you can proceed to the next dungeons. Collect other items for bonus points and avoid other knights that will shoot at you, even when their backs are turned. To make it fair, you can shoot them. Some knights only take one hit to kill, others may take more.

games.name: Cavelon 64
games.overview: Can you get the balloon through the hazardous caves of Morgor?

games.name: Cavelon II
games.overview:
Cavelon II is a sequel to Cavelon, and once again you must collect the door pieces to go to the next dungeon, and time is against you. When you have collected all the door pieces, you proceed to the next dungeon. This time though, other knights are not just your enemies. The Black Wizard will appear and release hazards such as birds and archers onto you. You can use ladders to get to other platforms. Also, you can jump over hazards, but not shoot them. If you're lucky, getting the Excalibur floating around will allow you to ride an unicorn, allowing you to easily avoid obstacles. When you are hit by an enemy, you lose a life. Lose all your lives, the game ends.

The game was re-released by Mastertronic in 1985 under the name Excaliba.

games.name: Caveman (Compute!)
games.overview: Caveman is a single-screen, single player platformer where your goal is to either avoid or beat the attacking dinosaurs and ptetosaurs with your trusty bat. It was originally published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1990/11.

games.name: Caveman Ugh-Lympics
games.overview:
Olympic Games set in the stone age. Events include clubbing, dino-racing, fire-making, mate-tossing, saber racing and the dino vault.

Supporting up to six players, you must select your caveman from a total of six different characters with different backgrounds, all with different skills and drawbacks.

versions.label: Caveman Ugh lympics (1988)(Electronic Arts)[cr Riffs Heptagon]
Caveman Ugh lympics (1988)(Electronic Arts)[cr Beyond Force]

games.name: Cavemania
games.overview: Fed up with having Brontosaurus steaks for dinner, Ug the Caveman has decided to try something new for a change - by navigating nine islands in search of the three pterodactyl eggs perched high in the mountains, and bringing them back to his cave one by one, making sure that not one egg breaks along the way. Unfortunately, searching for the eggs comes at a price. Ug must also leap across rivers, dodge erupting volcanoes, and use a number of rocks to kill any land-based predators that get in his way. If he comes into contact with any of these, he will lose some energy, which can be restored by collecting fruit. Once Ug has taken all three eggs to his cave, he has to collect some wheels so that he can travel to the next island.

games.name: Cavern Construction Kit
games.overview: A horizontally scrolling cave shooter, much like Skramble. You control a ship armed with bombs and air-to-air missiles with the mission of penetrating enemy territory, inflicting as many losses as possible on your opponents and hoard up treasures. Some might call it a suicide mission because of the multitude of various enemies including missiles, lasers, radar stations and boulders, and you must keep an eye on fuel consumption and fill up the tank by bombing any tanks in your path. A very special feature of the game is the ability to modify the landscape and to add and remove enemies as desired to increase or lower the challenge level.

games.name: Cavern Fighter
games.overview:
Professor R. Szymanski has injected an accelerator and DNA into your brain to make you more intelligent. Just as the DNA was at the required level there was an explosion in the lab which sent the Professor into a coma. He was the only one who knew how to stop the experiment so a navy assault ship is shrunk and injected into your blood stream to go and stop the DNA from growing. Eight pieces of a growth inhibitor must be collected before facing your brain. With a foreign body in your blood, blood cells and other parts of your body are trying to destroy you. You must battle these to hopefully get to the brain and stop your brain from exploding. Another hindrance is the fact that you have to find all the inter-cellular junctions to move about the body. Some require keys. Plasma spheres can be found along the way to upgrade your ship and weapons. DNA warrior is a horizontally side-scrolling shoot-em-up. The joystick will steer your ship while the fire button will fire your weapon. Pressing the space bar will select your next upgrade when a plasma sphere is collected. Also seen on the screen is a energy gauge, score and a ship upgrade to select. 

Published in New Special PlayGames N.20 (Maggio 1989)

games.name: Cavern of Riches
games.overview:
Adventure 1: Cavern of Riches is a typical text adventure game in which the player must try to collect the twelve different treasures hidden in the game world. They must be returned to their proper place.

The player can move around in all directions and can pick-up and manipulate items. Simple puzzles must be solved, but there is little to no story. The game does feature a save and load system to restore from an earlier game.

games.name: Cavern Run 64
games.overview: In Cavern Run 64 you move a spacecraft viewed from the side, left or right as it falls down a constantly scrolling cavern and you must avoid hitting the walls or it is game over. Before you play you can select your fuel level and this decreases, which is shown on the right of the screen, but there are fuel capsules that can be collected to increase your levels. Once you crash then you are told your distance traveled before you play again to beat your last score.

games.name: Caverns of Carnage
games.overview:
A shooter from the book "Time lost", created by Kirk Ostby and programmed by Joseph C. Giarratano for the C64. Jacque and Erin are in the fearsome and eerie Caverns of Carnage, attacked by the savage Crusher beasts. How long can they survive the Chase that no one has ever gotten 
through? How far can YOU get them through the caverns? 

In this game, Jacque is on the right and Erin on the left. Jacque’s Positron Blaster will destroy the loathsome Crushers and score points for each one disintegrated. You get more points the closer they are when you blast them. Each new cavern is narrower and more treacherous than the previous one, but you score more points. Watch out—if a Crusher gets Jacque or Erin from the front or if they crash into a wall or Crusher, the game is over. 
Use the “S” key to move them left, the “D” key to move them right and hold the space bar to fire.

games.name: Caverns of Doom
games.overview:
In the year 6502 BC, Jesmon Hys from the city of Nodlon discovered the ancient Tombs of Ledromica in the rich pastures of Tatseclus. Over the years of exploring the Tombs, Jesmon has discovered apart from treasures, that somewhere deep in the Tombs is a Temple dedicated to the worship of Rah. Too old to search for the Temple, Jesmon has written down his findings for the person who discovers them to continue his search for the Temple.

You play the role of Cuthbert who has discovered the writings of Jesmon and has decided to enter the Tombs to find treasure as well as the Temple. The game is a flick-screen maze game where you must search the various screens collecting treasure and bonuses while avoiding the monsters. You are armed and one shot is only needed to remove the monsters who appear after a few seconds after you enter a screen. Touching a monster loses you a life and you can only fire sideways. There are also doors that need opening with keys but you can only carry one key at a time.

versions.label: Caverns of Doom (1984)(Superior Graphics Emporium)[cr GP]

games.name: Caverns of Eriban
games.overview: You are the pilot of a mine supply ship and it is your task to deliver supplies to various amount of subterranean mining depots scattered deep in the Caverns of Eriban. Picking up five supplies and re-fuelling your ship on one of five landing strips on the surface at the entrance to the caverns, you must negotiate the passages to deliver your goods. As you explore the caverns looking for the depots you must avoid or shoot various obstacles and if you touch these obstacles or the walls then you lose one of eight lives. You also need to take account of the momentum of the craft as you move it with the joystick. The depots are represented by a small tower and each has a flashing light with red indicating it requires supplies while green means it's has supplies. You land your ship on a small landing strip next to the tower but land too fast and the ship is destroyed. Once you have delivered five supplies or your fuel is getting low then you have to make your way back to the surface and pick up five more to deliver.

versions.label: Caverns of Eriban, The (1985)(Firebird)[cr Flash Voodoo]
Caverns of Eriban, The (1985)(Firebird)[cr NO][t +4 NO]

games.name: Caverns of Jupiter
games.overview: A racing game where the goal is to stay safely on the track without hitting the edge.

versions.label: Caverns of Jupiter (1984)(Neil Tuddenham & Ian Robertson)

games.name: Caverns of Khafka
alt_names: Caverns of Khafka: Die Grabkammern des Pharao
games.overview:
Find 5 holy seals in a labyrinth and attach them to the gate at the temple of Pharao Khafka to open the gate. Enter the tomb, outwit the ghost guards and get the treasure. . . . .

This sounds easy, but it is not, because the people of the pharao does not live any more but all lockings and traps still work well. Furthermore, evil bugs, rolling and falling rocks, magma and bats obstruct the search. And finally, some tunnels and channels are very narrow so that our brave treasure hunter (or tomb raider) must crawl through them to avoid hurting his head.

In the unlikely event that you find all seals and get to the guards of the treasure, the most dagnerous task will follow, as you need to pass the guard without touching it. If this succeeds the adventurer will be awarded the Treasure of the Pharao, if not he will die a cruel death. . .

games.name: Caverns of Sillahc
games.overview: The Torms and the invading Humans don't like each other. Spotting a quick buck you have decided to take both sides. The Torms have taken the Humans' farming robots who want them back. The Humans want the Torms' power plant to be destroyed forcing them up to the surface. Your aim is to rescue the robots and navigate the underground caverns to destroy the power plant. The game is viewed from the side as you move your ship about with the joystick. Gravity influences the ship and almost the entire environment is deadly to the touch, so regular upwards thrust (requiring fuel) and careful steering is required. The ship is armed with a cannon to take out mines and clear blocked passages. Attention must be paid to how many robots are picked up - too many means you crash. Some of the landing pads robots must be delivered to double as fuel stops.

games.name: Caverns of Xydrahpur
games.overview: On the planet Rydthar, the inhabitants call themselves Earthlings and they have been forced to leave the planet and settle on the third moon, Xydrahpur. The Earthlings had built Absolute Control Stations (ACS) and placed them all over the planet but they have gone out of control taking over the planet. On their new home it is soon discovered that there is an active ACS deep in the caverns under the surface. A hero is needed to go down through the tunnels and deactivate the ACS and you play one such hero, Starman Jones. Caverns of Xydrahpur is a side view flick-screen game where you control Jones on his spacebike and move through the tunnels of the caverns to locate the ACS. On each screen there is an obstacle like an alien or gates that open and shut which need avoiding. If you touch an obstacle or the cavern walls then you lose one of five lives but you start on the last screen you were on.

games.name: Caves of 64
games.overview: Caves of 64 is a side view horizontal shooter where the screen scrolls from right to left constantly, and you control a spacecraft flying inside your Commodore 64 over various levels. The idea is to reach the CPU while flying through palaces and the BASIC and Kernal ROM. You must shoot or avoid various obstacles as well as avoid lasers or touching the walls or you lose one of three lives. Your craft has fuel which decreases as you fly but you can shoot fuel capsules to increase it. Parts of each level has different ways to fly but only one doesn't end up into a dead end where you have no option but to lose a life.

games.name: Caves of Silver
games.overview:
You were walking in the woods and came to the entrance of a cave covered by brush.

People say that many years ago, Long John Silver hid his silver in the cave, but no one has found it.

versions.label: Caves of Silver(The Guild Adventure Software)

games.name: Caves of Venus
games.overview: A space platformer game by Marc E.H. Dawson & Robert W. Tinman that takes place in the Caves of Venus, naturally. It has a relationship with The Nodes of Yesod, which wasn't programmed by Robert W. Tinman, but the sequel Arc of Yesod was, though CSDB shows that The Nodes of Yesod was an update over Caves of Venus, Yesod was published before the release of this game. This is possible as release could be years after creation but it is interestingly circuitous and publication is always another layer of complication and can take much longer.

versions.label: Caves of Venus(Odin Computer Graphics)[cr DR]

games.name: Celebrity Squares
games.overview:
The 4th sample game from The Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit by Sensible Software
Created with the Kit by Gary Penn & Gary Liddon.

games.name: Cell Defense
games.overview: An education game based on a cellular science simulation and biology properties.

games.name: Cell Mates
games.overview:
Created by William K. Balthrop and published in Home Computer Magazine Vol.5, No.6, the game asks the question, how complex is a living cell? Is it a static structure— or a dynamic system? How do symbiotic organisms make all cellular life possible? Find some answers with this fascinating bio-simulation. There is more going on inside a living cell than meets the eye. Even the most powerful microscopes have not yet revealed the entire 
story— the secret life of the cell. Ask most people what they know about this basic life unit, and their reply, if any, may invoke a static picture of the cell and its interior: the cell wall, the nucleus, and "a bunch of little floaty things." But when biologists look closer at these little floaty things, they see participants in an incredibly complex, wonderfully cooperative, and dynamic ecosystem; for the metabolism of a living cell involves some strange and alien participants who apparently learned to live together millions of years ago. Directing this metabolic dance, communicating with each cell part through encoded molecules, is the nucleus. Some of the participants— called organelles— possess their own DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) and reproduce themselves independently from the nucleus. Together, they are all Cell Mates.  
 
The program presents the actual playing screen. This screen contains a graphics representation of the cell (in the upper-left corner), and 12 indicators that show the status of the various processes in the cell. You can gauge your progress by viewing these indicators. Some of the indicators contain areas highlighted against the background color. To maintain and eventually reproduce the cell, you must manipulate the cell's life processes so that the pointers remain in these "safe" areas. Indicators that contain no distinguished area show the actual level of energy 
going to specific activities.

games.name: Cell Runner
games.overview:
Cross over to the other side by stepping on the "cells" However make sure you don't run out of time or step onto the wrong cell or it's game over. 

This game was written by John Krutch and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/09 (Issue #39) as well as in Stonysoft #0343.

games.name: Cells & Serpents
games.overview:
Go adventuring in the meanest, darkest, most definitely fatal set of dungeons you ever waved a sword around! There re more monsters than you ever dared to have nightmares about. Fancy meeting a Mind Flayer for instance? How about being sized up by an Intellect Devourer? If you live long enough (doubtful) and might just get to shake hands with Asmodeus! Once only mind...
There is great gold and glory to be had here, but be very, very careful where you tread! You can save your game unto tape at any point if it all gets too much and carry on once you've recovered your nerve...
Find out how good you really are at adventure with this frantic fantasy frolic. Not for the faint of heart or slow of sword.

The game: Cells and Serpents is an adventure game set in an underground labyrinth of rooms. Each of these may contain one of an enormous variety of monsters (which could kill you), treasure or artifacts (which will increase your wealth or magical and physical capabilities). Your aim is to collect as much treasure as possible by delving deeper and deeper into the maze...and staying alive!

games.name: Celluloid
games.overview: A Breakout/Arkanoid style game released in Game On 1990/10, and also in Abo Disk #2.

games.name: Celtix
games.overview: Celtix is a miscellaneous single-player shooter for the Commodore 64. The game was developed by 59 Productions and published in Loadstar #157.

games.name: Centauri Alliance
games.overview: Describing Centauri Alliance as "The Bard’s Tale in Space" would be fitting since it was designed by Michael Cranford, the creator of the first two Bard's Tale games. In this science-fiction RPG, players build a party by designing characters from six different races and arming them with a variety of weapons and psychic powers. They then set off across a cluster of star systems on a secret mission to find a powerful super-weapon and save the worlds of the Alliance from evil forces. The game contains most of the standard RPG elements of late '80s games including first person 10' X 10' square adventuring maps, turn-based combat and an ongoing quest to find bigger and better ways to kill things.

games.name: Centipede
games.overview: The player moves the character about the bottom area of the screen and fires laser shots at a centipede advancing from the top of the screen down through a field of mushrooms. Shooting any section of the centipede creates a mushroom; shooting one of the middle segments splits the centipede into two pieces at that point. Each piece then continues independently on its way down the board, with the first section of the rear piece becoming a new head. If the head is destroyed, the section behind it becomes the next head.

games.name: Centipede 2025
games.overview: From the looks of it, possibly one of the best games of the Big 100. A Centipede clone released as part of "Arcadepack" by Multisoft, also a  game of "The Big 100" collection and released in the S+S Soft Demodiskette.

games.name: Centric
games.overview: A very nicely done Tron\Lightcycle style game developed by Cynace and published in 64'er 1996/12.

games.name: Centripod
games.overview: Released as part of "Arcade Games II" pack. The Centripods are attacking, Dactoes are falling and Caruths are hopping in this fast action arcade game.

games.name: Centron
games.overview:
Head to head top to bottom Pong! A game much like tennis but with a metal ball intended to be played by two people, each with their own joysticks. The ball will be brought into play from the center of the court, suddenly arising from a large ball that appears to be similar to a planet. The direction of the ball will be random to begin. Good luck and happy gaming!

This game was released in Italy under the name Pingor in both Hit Parade C64 n.71 (Ottobre 1992) and Special Program n.88 (giugno 1992).

versions.label: Centron (1991)(Blue Chip Software)[cr The Burp Boyz]

games.name: Centropods
games.overview: Centropods is a single screen shooter viewed from the side inspired by the arcade game Centipede where you control a craft at the bottom of the screen and you must shoot and destroy a Centropod. You are able to move your craft left or right as well as forwards and backwards a short distance. The Centropd appears at the top of the screen and moves across and when it hits a sticky glue pod or the edge of the screen then it lowers one place and changes direction. When you hit the Centropod then it splits into two and further shooting keeps splitting it until it is finally destroyed. The sticky glue pods are scattered in great numbers around the screen and can be removed after various shots to receive bonus points. Also on screen are a spinning alien buzzer which moves around the screen and a hovering saucer which moves across the screen and when shot gets you more bonus points. Once the Centropod has been destroyed then another one appears and this keeps happening until you run out of lives. If you touch the Centropod, buzzer or saucer then you lose one of three lives.

games.name: Centurions: Power X Treme
games.overview: The Centurions are Ace McCloud, Jake Rockwell and Max Ray. They must battle the forces of Doc Terror to stop his attempts at infiltrating the Weapons Development Centre and run off with a large supply of Tyron Dichromate, a chemical used in Nuclear Fusion.
