With only 250 treasures to locate and collect by 10 players, the treasure soon goes so the game resets. Any treasure you do not have in the swamp is lost forever.

The game is played in the style of a text-adventure with no graphics. Putting in commands directs your character who can interact with the other players. The game is played in real-time as you watch characters come and go in one location.

games.name: Micro Olympics
games.overview: Eleven Track 'N' Field style events are recreated in this joystick-waggling based game. Five are simple running events of different distances ranging from 100 meters to 1500 meters. Unlike Daley Thompson's Decathlon the longer events don't involve a different technique, or different performance measurements, making the 1500m quite tiring. There are also three throwing events (Javelin, Discus and Hammer), and the High / Long / Triple Jump events. Each event has a pre-defined world record to chase.

games.name: Micro Rescue
games.overview:
This was a "tape loader game" which was a very small game that could be loaded into memory and played while you waited for the main game on the tape to load. Commodore tape load times could be close to 30 minutes in some cases. The object of the game is to rescue six stranded men from the surface of the planet and return them to the mother ship before the main game has loaded.

The game was a clone of Taito's Lunar Rescue.

games.name: Microchess #3
games.overview: the first version of Microchess was published in 1977 for various CP/M and Z80 machines and was ported to the Commodore PET/CBM a year later. So the first version of PETChess for the C64 was pretty much ready to run even before the machine debuted. This updated game is a graphically improved, and faster version of that first port and it does a pretty good job, without too many slowdown, especially when run from floppy.

games.name: Microcosm
games.overview: Microcosm is a single screen platformer where you control the Maintenance Engineer, on the crippled interstellar freightliner Nimbus, as you attempt to save the priceless cargo Terran Plant over various levels. You must walk or fly with your jet-pack around the screen and pick up seeds, one at a time from the top of the screen and feed it to the various stalks by walking over them. Once all the stalks are fully grown then you move to the next level to grow more stalks. Aphids move around the screen and these can be shot with your laser or avoided and if you touch one then you lose one of three lives. Acid drops fall down the screen and must be avoided and on later levers there are spiders and bugs that cannot be shot just avoided and if touched lose a life.

games.name: Microdot
games.overview:
A fantastically odd little maze game, Microdot involves rolling a ball around a series of screens with the purpose of collecting radioactive particles. The game is similar to Jet Set Willy but it's simple graphical style, fast play-speed and the inclusion of a level editor set this one apart from the rest. On the few occasions I got to play on my mate's C64, this was the game that impressed me the most.
 
Published in several compilations and publications including Commodore Disk User 1989/01-02, Your Commodore 1990/01 (Tape #01), and in Your Commodore 1991/10 (Tape #22).

games.name: MicroLeague Baseball
games.overview: Microleague eschew action in favor of strategy for this licensed baseball game. The real-life teams and players are included, as well as classic teams from the past - lots of data disks were released featuring additional lineups. Each play is graphically shown, with a running commentary detailing how it unfolds. A wide range of strategies are available. You can bring the stand-in players in, and instruct players as to how aggressively to play when opportunities arise, with 7 distinct batting strategies. When fielding you have options on field placement and bowling style - use the fastball and curveball wisely. Players will sometimes pick up injuries (the correct level of warming up can reduce this risk), or argue with the umpire over controversial decisions.

games.name: MicroLeague Baseball: Box Score Stats Compiler Disk
games.overview: An add on to the primary game that allows box scores to compiled automatically for the teams you store for the entire season of play with other MicroLeague teams. See your whole season's stats all in one place and print them out to review later.

versions.label: MicroLeague Baseball Box Score Stats Compiler Disk (1986)(Microleague Sports)

games.name: MicroLeague Baseball II
games.overview: MicroLeague Baseball II is a baseball managerial simulation game. The player takes the role of a major league manager. There are actual stats for pitching, hitting, fielding, running and more. The games features an exclusive "Quick-Play" Option Menu as well as powerhouse teams from the past and present.

games.name: MicroLeague Football: The Coach's Challenge
games.overview:
MicroLeague Football: The Coach's Challenge is an American football simulation where you play as a head coach of a team.

Before the game, you have to select the home and visiting team (both could be played by either human or computer), and make roster changes if you wish. During the game the human player can call the plays and pick the pass patterns, make substitutions for injuries etc. It is also possible to play a 'quick' game displaying just the results that could be printed. Release includes "General Manager / Owner Disk".

versions.label: MicroLeague Football (1990)(Microleague Sports)[cr NEC Ikari Talent]

games.name: MicroLeague Wrestling
games.overview:
MicroLeague Wrestling is a wrestling game, the very first one licensed by the World Wrestling Federation. The game can be played by one or two players and comes with two possible match-ups, each with a separate match disk. 

There is Hulk Hogan versus "Macho Man" Randy Savage (all platforms) A bout can last 10, 20 or 60 minutes.

Game presentation before, during, and after fights is modeled after WWF TV shows and features digitized stills of actual WWF personalities, including wrestlers, managers, interviewers, commentators and announcers. Digitized images illustrate on-camera interviews, the wrestlers' entrances (complete with renditions of their themes), ringside commentary, and the reactions of the crowd.

During a fight, the game follows an unusual approach: Instead of controlling a wrestler directly, players select a move to perform from a menu. The computer decides if it was a success or not and the result is shown via a digitized picture.

versions.label: Commodore 64: MicroLeague Wrestling (1988)(Micro League Sports Association)

games.name: Middle Earth Quiz
games.overview: A rather tough, multiple choice Middle Earth Quiz published in Loadstar #002.

games.name: Midnight Resistance
games.overview: The player takes control of a commando who is out to rescue his kidnapped family, including his scientist grandfather who is being forced to create a weapon which will give the antagonist of the game, known only as "the Commissar", the power to take over the Earth. In the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis version, the commando, known as Johnny Ford is on a solo mission to destroy the reign of the entity known as "The Crimson King" who kidnapped his family because Johnny's Father, Malcolm Ford created a serum which could make people immune to the addicting effects of drugs.

versions.label: Midnight Resistance (1990)(Ocean)[cr ILS][f NTSC Random][t +6 ILS]
Midnight Resistance (1990)(Ocean)[cr Mr. Fox][t 5M Mr. Fox]

games.name: Midway Campaign
games.overview: Midway Campaign is a computer simulation of the Battle of Midway Island in June 1942, arguably one of the most decisive battles in the history of warfare. The computer controls a huge force of Japanese ships whose objective is to invade and capture Midway Island. You command the badly outnumbered and outraged American forces with your only advantage being the element of surprise. The game ends if either all of one side's Aircraft Carriers are sunk, or any part of Japanese TF exits map to west or US TF exits map to east with no airstrikes in the air. At the end of the game a summary of all carrier damage, aircraft losses, and victory points from other targets and the Midway invasion are output followed by an evaluation of results.

games.name: Mieyen
games.overview: Destroy the ghosts in the maze before they eat all the burgers. The ghosts are invisible unless you have a direct line of sight to them, but you can often work out where they are by watching the food disappear piece by piece.

games.name: MiG-29 Soviet Fighter
games.overview: The player plays the role of a Soviet MiG-29 fighter pilot. The object of the game is to defeat the World Terrorist Army. It is similar in style to After Burner. MiG-29 cartridges have a small switch in the back to make the game compatible with U.S. and European systems.

versions.label: Mig 29 Soviet Fighter (1989)(Codemasters)[cr Austrian Cracking Crew]

games.name: MiG Alley Ace
games.overview:
MiG Alley Ace is an action-based simulation of air combat during the Korean War. The titular MiG Alley was the area over North Korea near the Chinese border where the world's first large-scale jet-to-jet air battles took place, with, among others, the American F-86 Sabre facing off against the Soviet MiG-15 Fagot.

The game is similar to MicroProse's earlier simulations Hellcat Ace and Spitfire Ace. MiG Alley Ace differs in that it offers a two-player mode via split screen. Five different scenarios based on actual encounters from the war are available. Each can be played solo, cooperatively or head-to-head. The goal in each scenario is to shoot down as many of the enemy planes as possible before the own squadron is destroyed. If a player's plane is destroyed but other craft from their squadron remain, they take control over one of the surviving planes. A scenario can result in a victory or loss for either side (or a neutral result in case the time limit expires). What the result is depends on a number of factors - while a destroyed enemy plane always nets victory points, the enemy might not be punished for it if the pilot bailed out or ditched the plane. Losing a scenario deducts from the player's lives: too many losses means the game has to be restarted.

games.name: Might and Magic: Book One
alt_names: Might and Magic: Book One - Secret of the Inner Sanctum
Might and Magic: Secret of the Inner Sanctum
games.overview:
Might and Magic is the first dungeon-crawling role-playing video game in the long-running series. The plot focuses on six adventurers in a quest to discover the secret of the "Inner Sanctum," though little information is offered upfront about this quest or its object. The ultimate quest is kept intentionally vague, and left for players to gradually piece together as they explore the world. 
Although it appears to take place in a straightforward medieval fantasy setting of knights in armor, mythical monsters and magicians, a number of science fiction elements are revealed later in the game,

versions.label: Might and Magic Book One Secret of the Inner Sanctum (1988)(New World Computing)
Might and Magic Book One Secret of the Inner Sanctum v2.0 (1987)(New World Computing)

games.name: Might and Magic II
alt_names: Might and Magic Book Two: Gates to Another World
Might and Magic: Gates to Another World
Might and Magic II: Gates to Another World
games.overview:
The space traveler and rogue guardian Sheltem has left the world VARN, where he was pursued by the relentless Corak the Mysterious and a party of local adventurers helping him. The Gates to Another World eventually takes all of them to another world, known as CRON. There, a great turmoil is caused by Sheltem's actions, and the heroes must stop his madness, preventing him from casting the planet into its own sun.

Gates to Another World is the second installment in the Might and Magic series, and a sequel to Secret of the Inner Sanctum. Core gameplay is similar to predecessor, with the player creating a party of six characters and exploring vast first-person 3D environments, while fighting enemies in turn-based combat and leveling up. Unlike the first game, enemy encounters occur at set points rather than spawning randomly, though enemy type selection is still random.

Like in the previous game, character classes rely each on a particular attribute to be effective. Knight, Paladin, Archer, Cleric, Sorcerer and Robber return, with the addition of two new classes, Ninja and Barbarian. Race selection features humans, elves, dwarves, gnomes, and half-orcs. There are several locations and items that are restricted to certain genders, alignments, or races. A new feature is the possibility to hire two non-player characters to travel with the party and participate in battles. A new skill system is introduced as well, allowing characters to learn such abilities as mountaineering (necessary to traverse mountains), linguist (for reading certain messages), cartographer (for creating an auto-map), and others.

Compared to the first game, the sequel is more quest-oriented, with various characters in towns giving quests to the party, as opposed to purely exploration-based traveling in the predecessor. Time also plays a large role in this game, with some instances requiring the party to travel to different time periods. Characters also age as the game goes on; If the player waits too long, the characters' statistics will change to reflect their aging, and they will eventually die.

versions.label: Might and Magic Book Two Gates to Another World (1989)(New World Computing)

games.name: Mighty Bombjack
games.overview: The sequel to the original Bomb Jack, Mighty Bombjack brings side scrolling to the series, and brings it closer to a platform game rather than the arcade / puzzle likeness of the first one. Once again you play as the bomb-hungry caped superhero. Collect the bombs for points and avoid being touched by the different monsters that spawn from crates and the like. The game now features new scenarios like clouds and forests, as well as the usual sphinx and pyramids backgrounds of the original title.

versions.label: Mighty Bombjack (1991)(Elite)[cr Legend][f NTSC PAL NEI][t +2 Legend]

games.name: Mike Gunner
games.overview:
You are Mike Gunner, the most effective detective in the country, who has been hired to end with all the criminals of Robbland city, perhaps the most dangerous city on Earth. You must have very warm nerves, very cold head and especially the most prepared to pull the trigger.

Mike Gunner is a shooting-gallery Operation Wolf-style game, requiring the Gun Stick accessory. The player will have to adjust the contrast and brightness of your screen, in order to gain optimum performance.

Thorough the game you will find people who shouldn't shot at: for example kids or policemen, all of them easily identifiable. But be careful, others will appear disguised as peaceful musicians, and in the least expected moment they will show they are not so friendly.

games.name: Mike Read's Computer Pop Quiz
games.overview:
BBC Radio 1 DJ Mike Read presented a pop music quiz show, which is recreated here with questions from the 50s to the 80s. You can play against the computer or another human; either way, select a specialist subject and 2 team-mate graphics (all representing white people). The overall style and presentation are very similar to Elite's earlier A Question of Sport license.

In the first round you select one of twelve random questions from the Jukebox, each of which has four options. A correct answer earns you two points, while an incorrect answer gives your opponent the chance to steal for one point. In round 2 you get three clues to name a star - you get three points for guessing from one clue, two points from two, and one point if you need all 3. In round three, choose an Easy question (from your category) for one point, or a Hard one (from someone else's) for two.

Round four asks you to Guess The Year that a set of events happened in, with scoring the same as round 2. Then comes the quickfire round - answer up to nine questions in 45 seconds, with a 2-second penalty for an incorrect answer. Finally, the six remaining Jukebox pictures are revealed and answered.

versions.label: Mike Read's Computer Pop Quiz (1989)(Elite)[cr Action]
Mike Read's Computer Pop Quiz (1989)(Elite)[cr Matrix]
Mike Read's Computer Pop Quiz (1989)(Elite)[cr Hotline INC]
Mike Read's Computer Pop Quiz (1989)(Elite)[cr HTL+INC]

games.name: Mike the Cave-Man
games.overview: Odd little platformer made in BASIC released by Klaus-Dieter Frohn and published in both 64'er Sonderheft 66, and in 64'er 1999/01. Mike the Caveman: An archaeologist is desperately looking for the exit from the old pyramid before he runs out of air. Find the right path away and save Mike! The archaeologist Dr. Mike Holehead has himself trapped in the catacombs of the Chenon Pyramid. Help him get back to daylight!

games.name: Mikie
games.overview:
Mikie puts you in charge of Mikie, a high school student who likes to win hearts of every girl that he can lay his eyes on.

There are several classrooms to explore like the Quantum Physics Room, Locker Room, Canteen, the Aerobics Dancing Class, and the Playground. In each classroom, Mikie has to collect all the hearts that are found in each classroom to form a message. In order to collect these hearts, Mikie must stand somewhere near them and shout out. There are two type of hearts: small and large. Mikie needs to shout out only once to collect the small hearts, and multiple times to collect the large ones. When a message is formed, Mikie can exit the classroom through a door marked OUT.

Stopping him from collecting the hearts is the teacher, the chef, and the janitor. The teacher is the worst one. When he is unable to catch you, he works up a sweat, and eventually, throws his teeth at you. When his teeth hits Mikie, he loses one of his three lives. In later classrooms, Mikie can throw stuff at his enemies in order to stun them for several seconds (for instance, the basketballs in the locker room, and the chickens in the canteen). The janitor isn't as bad because he walks much slower than the others.

In between levels, you have to enter the next classroom through a door marked IN without being caught, but you can do at least two things to pass time: Steal some lunch, and open one of the unmarked doors to receive a punch, a kick, or the chance to see a naked lady with breasts. Beware that if you take too long in the hallway and don't travel between floors, a bucket slides across the screen real fast and attempt to slip you.

If you're good enough at the game, you can enter a high score, and if you fail to enter anything, the game will assume that you are Clint Eastwood.

games.name: Military Coup
games.overview:
Military Coup is a strategy game for one player where you attempt to take over a city from the current Government run by President Xerxes, by trying to take over the streets and prominent buildings. There are five skill levels to choose from as well as the type of Government you want to take over and the type you will be if you succeed and they are Communist, Socialist, Liberal, Rightwing and Fascist. After your choices, you are shown a list of the 15 prominent buildings which include a Radio Station, Airport, Hospital and Cathedral. The President's Palace is also included but the chances of taking this over is very slim. The list of buildings also show which side they would support and the likelihood of changing sides which changes every game.

You now see a map of the city shown on the whole screen in the form of squares on a 11 x 7 grid with each square representing a street and the buildings in neutral grey. You now have four moves to take over either a street or a building and you can get a intelligence report on a building for free. If you succeed in a takeover then the building or street turns into your colour which is either red or blue, but if you fail then you lose all your remaining turns. Once your go is over, the computer now attempts to takeover, and when finished you are shown the news and other buildings or streets can change colour or change sides after both goes are completed. You keep selecting buildings and streets and you can select ones that the computer owns. Points are awarded for certain successful moves and the winner of the game is the first to 35 points.

games.name: Milk Race
games.overview:
The Milk Race involved cycling 1000 miles across Britain, and the game simulates being one of the 84 entrants. The route takes you form Newcastle to London via Sheffield, Birmingham and Ipswich among others.

The roads are strewn with potholes, and cars and other bikes make things more treacherous. Time-trials are sprung on you at random, and these must be completed in the allotted time.

You can’t cycle at full pelt for the whole event and you need to make efficient use of energy, via pacing yourself and riding in higher gears when you reach hills, are vital. Milk (what else?) can be picked up to boost your energy.

games.name: Mill Mania
games.overview: A two-player only betting/gambling game where you will only have virtual losses. Music by Thomas Bendt & Mario Kriwanek.

games.name: Millenium Warriors
games.overview: According to ancient Iridani law, the first born son of the Great Galactic Emperor has to participate in a Test of Arms to become Prince of the Southern Nebular and become first in line to the throne. You are Prince Kronos and your father is Iridon I and the time has come for you to take the test which means being transported to the toughest battlefield in the Universe, Earth. You have to visit five time zones and fight an opponent from each era in a one-on-one fight with a weapon to pass the test. The time zones are Caveman, Knights, Arabian, Pirates and a final battle in space. Each fight is seen from the side with each zone shown on the whole of the screen. There are two styles of game, a beat-em-up or a shooter. The Caveman, Knights and Pirates zones are all beat-em-ups and sees your hero with a weapon from that era. You have one attack but you can defend your opponents attacks as well. The Arabian and Space are shooters with each fighter facing each other on a magic carpet or wearing a jet-pack. Fireballs or lasers are fired at each other and when an opponent is beaten in a zone then you move to the next one until all are defeated. As the fights progress, there are three gauges to keep an eye on, Energy, Health and Weapon. The Energy gauge decreases every time you move or use your weapon. When you stop moving or using your weapon then it slowly increases. The Health gauge decreases every time you are hit by your opponent but items appear on screen which can be collected to increase it and you can also collect items to increase your energy. When either gauge have reached zero then you lose the fight but you get two more attempts to defeat your opponent. The weapon gauge will decrease when you use your weapon. When this reaches zero then you lose your weapon and leave you defenceless but one will appear and can be collected. Before you play the game there are various options that can be selected. Once fights have been won then that zone can be selected, you can choose your difficulty level (1-3), and either a one, two player game or a demo. Two player game sees you fighting in each zone and once a victor has emerged then both players fight in the next zone.

games.name: Millennium Assault
games.overview: Based on the Star Wars films, this shoot-em-up is a Star Wars related game you may be unaware of, however feels like more work was put into the music than the game itself. It was developed by Cosine Systems (The late Jason Kelk did the code and graphics, and Gareth Dolloway did the SFX and music) Published in Commodore Zone Issue #11.

games.name: Millie-Bug
games.overview: Millie-Bug is a single screen shooter based on the arcade game Centipede where you control a spacecraft on the bottom of the screen attempting to destroy a Millibug that appears at the top. You are able to move left or right, forwards a short distance, and backwards as you keep firing upwards to hit the Millibug. If the Millibug is hit then it splits into two moving in different directions and if any of the bug hits the side of the screen or a mushroom then it moves down one place and moves in the opposite direction. The screen is full of mushrooms which cannot be passed but will disappear when hit by a few shots from you. Other creatures make an appearance like spiders and snails and these can be avoided or shot for bonus points. If the bug hits the bottom of the screen then it starts to make its way back up the screen. If you touch the bug or any other creature then you lose one of three lives. Before the game you can select a skill level from one to nine.

games.name: Millionaire: The Stock Market Simulation
games.overview:
In the game you are starting a session at the U.S. stock market with a beginning net worth equal to $10,000. Three companies from Computer, Oil & Gas, Retail Sales, Auto, and Heavy Industries are present on this market. Stock prices are changing each week due to economical, political, or social situations. On each turn you should examine the news and trends, and buy or sell a certain quantity of stocks in order to increase your net worth. Based on your net worth, you'll be classified by one of the five ranks: Novice, Investor, Speculator, Professional, or Broker. The higher rank you have, the more investment opportunities are available to you. The goal is to finish the session with as a high a net worth as possible; the highest rank is Millionaire.

The game is available for single player and the game may be saved to be restored later.

versions.label: Millionaire The Stock Market Simulation (1984)(Blue Chip Software)

games.name: Mind Control
games.overview:
Mind Control is a single screen game split into two parts where your mission is to destroy Zyco, an indestructible alien who is ruling Earth and enslaving all humans. Scientists realising that Zyco can't be destroyed, have worked out that his only weak spot would be the massive sensory neurone in his brain and so have selected you to be shrunk to enter his bloodstream to move around his brain before destroying the neurone with a laser. The first part of the game is a platformer where you must get from the bottom right of the screen and climb stairs at each end of the three levels that make up the screen to get to Zyco's brain. Trying to stop you are people and these have to be jumped or if you touch them, then you lose one of three lives. At the top of the screen is a Miniaturising Room where you are shrunk before you enter the brain.

The second part of the game has you viewing the brain from the side and you have to make your way from the bottom of the screen to the centre of the brain following a path. As you move around the brain there are white blood corpuscles and anti-bodies following a set path and these must be avoided or you increase in size and a life is lost. The walls that make up the path also make you grow if touched so these have to be avoided as well. Once you reach the center and destroy the neurone you then keep attempting to move around the brain over various levels where the enemies get faster.

The ACE release doesn't have the first platform part of the game, just the moving around the brain part.

games.name: Mind Games
games.overview: Published in Commodore Disk User 1988/07-08, as well as Your Commodore 1991/03 (Tape #15), and GO64! 2005/10. Explore the president's brain and find out what kind of guy is entrusted with the button to end all civilization. A summit conference of the world's two military giants is scheduled for tomorrow, but for no very good reason the US president has gone totally insane. Well, not totally insane, one coherent idea remains alive deep within his subconscious. It is your mission, should you accept it, to guide this small bubble of sanity through the labyrinth of the president's mind, destroying insane thoughts and opening the doors of reason. Ultimately you must find the exit from his subconscious and enter the president's conscious mind, restoring his sanity. The president's subconscious is made up of a 10 x 16 grid of 256 rooms. Each room is full of insane thoughts which must be blasted. When a certain number of thoughts have been destroyed (this number is different for each room) the doors will begin to open. The player can then pass through these into the next room, and when the exit is reached, sanity is restored.

games.name: Mind Maze
games.overview: A puzzle game from Commodore Format 1995/02 (Issue #53). This is a puzzler to make your granny weep, your brain explode and your shrink-wrapped TV dinner spontaneously combust! With 32 levels of frenetic action, this one'll keep you going for months.

games.name: Mind Prober
games.overview: Personality Software That Lets You See People As They Really Are. Analyze anyone in your life. Get to know their secret likes and dislikes. Find out hidden truths about people you thought you knew Learn how to make the most of relationships and how to prevent emotional letdowns A self-help book\program on how to read others. Remember, it's not who you know, it's how well you know them.

games.name: Mind-Roll
games.overview:
You play a rolling eyeball in an attempt to find your way through numerous mazes. Each maze features different puzzles to solve and objects such as keys to collect in order to find the destination. There is a limited amount of time to solve each maze.

This game was known as Mind-Roll in the US. Quedex is the PAL name.

games.name: Mind-Stretchers
games.overview:
Mind-Stretchers is a compilation released for Amstrad CPC and Sinclair ZX Spectrum as well as C64. It contains the following three games:

-    Cluedo
-    Computer Scrabble
-    Monopoly

games.name: Mind Warp
games.overview: Your mission. To protect start Block Ceta Major from from Romulan and Klingon Menace!

games.name: Mindbender (Gremlin Graphics)
games.overview: Mindbender uses similar gameplay principles to Deflektor, which means that you have indirect control over a beam of light. On each of the 50 levels you must guide it from a starting point to an ending point, taking out all the enemies along the way. Rotating each of the many mirrors on the level to send the beam onto the points the enemies hover over does this – reaching many of them will involve several attempts at finding the right combination of angles. Rotating barriers, light bulb switches and locked sections must all be taken into account, but there are also magic balloons later on. All this must be done within a time limit, and directing the beam back into itself causes overloads and must be avoided, Tron-style.

games.name: Mindbreaker
games.overview: Mindbreaker is a memory/puzzle game developed by Century-Art Studios and published in Game On 1991/10.

games.name: Mindfighter
games.overview:
The computer game of an Anna Popkess book (which was originally bundled with the game) uses an interactive fiction System Without A Name, or SWAN for short. It’s set in a post-apocalyptic world of guards desperately attempting to retain order over mobs of genetically-mutated thugs, with extensive use of the death penalty.

Into this maelstrom steps Robin, an 11-year-old psychic beamed forward in time from before the drama. Adjusting to a completely different form of life, Robin must learn to survive and get adequate food, and ultimately infiltrate this vicious police state.

games.name: Mindshadow
games.overview:
At the beginning of Mindshadow you find yourself on a lonely beach in a lifeless hut. With a headache and no memory. 

The object of the game is to completely regain your memory. As you progress in the game a word or phrase will trigger memories of the past. Like most adventure games the fun of the game is centered on discovery of you and your surroundings.

games.name: Mindtrap
games.overview:
This abstract puzzler promises 999,999 different levels, with a game design bearing some relation to sliding-block games. You are presented with up to 24 coloured and spotted (like dice) blocks, arranged in columns of up to 4. The task is to arrange these so that they are lined up in columns matching their number.

You are in control of a crosshair, which can be moved to cover four blocks. Holding fire while pushing left or right and hovering it over a group of 4 will move the four blocks around in sequence. Things can get harder when the level arrangement results in blocks having to be moved through sections with a column of only 2, or when some parts of the arena lack cogs, meaning that you can't move on those sections. Later in the game you'll have to work on multiple floors at the same time, switching blocks between them.

games.name: Mindwarp
games.overview:
The Air Force has developed, in collaboration with a famous aeronaval construction company, a new aircraft that must be able, in the event of an attack by alien beings, to fight for the people of earth. But such a powerful and potent vehicle will be ineffective if good pilots capable of handling it are not trained. Since the conditions in which the aircraft will have to operate are for the moment still futuristic, the Air Force has built fantastic means to simulate the extraterrestrial attack and allow pilots to prepare. You too have had the opportunity to enter among these privileged ones and you have to demonstrate your skills in eliminating as many enemies as possible. 

Published in Italy as Fly in New Special PlayGames n.3 (novembre 1987) and in Hit Parade C64 n.22 (Aprile 1988).

games.name: Mindwheel
games.overview: This real time all-text game puts you in the role of a Mind Adventurer, asked to journey back through the minds of four deceased residents of your planet in search of the Wheel of Wisdom. The Wheel is the only thing that can restore your planet from the state of chaos it's now in. The hardbound book that comes with the game includes the instructions and a novella-length introduction to the plot.

games.name: Mine Canyon
games.overview:
Mine Canyon is an avoid-it game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by John Krutch and published by Ion International, Inc. in Ahoy! 1986/09 (Issue #33).

The game is also known under the names Run Throught and Lauf Durch!

games.name: Mine Field
games.overview: An unpublished Pac-Man styled collect-em-up game for 1 player from MSC in 1990. It would later be heavily reworked and updated and released as Techno Plyn.

games.name: Mine Sweeper 9000
games.overview: Mine Sweeper 9000 is a clone of classic Minesweeper. It allows to select difficulty level, customize board size, define controls, choose a background tune and save/load state of the game. All the other rules remain unchanged, including marking cells and mistake consequences.

games.name: Mine Sweeper (Compute!)
games.overview:
You'd think it was a "minesweeper" game by the title but its really a fast-paced and really tough shooter. Released as Strasdenian in Italy in International Games n.8 (settembre 1991).  
 
You are on patrol in the skies of Frekkel orbital station when aliens are spotted approaching. Thus begins your battle against the strange and menacing beings who want to conquer the world. You must fly (being careful not to hit the buildings) and destroy the aliens that appear on your dial with your laser cannon. You have to be very careful as they are very fast and often have unpredictable movements. At the end of the squadron of enemies you will have to face the Strasdenian support ship which is very powerful and must be hit many times to destroy. If you can get past the support ship make your way to a tougher level with a mothership at the end.

games.name: Minefield
games.overview: Minefield is a clone of classic Minesweeper. The gameplay rules remain unchanged. Selected spot shows the number of bombs in the neighborhood. There is no possibility to select any gameplay aspects. The player has limited time to finish the board - 1000 seconds.

games.name: Minefields
games.overview: An implementation of Minesweeper for the C64 created by Christoph Cemper with music and SFX by Patrick Peters and published as part of Game On 1993/04.

games.name: Miner!
games.overview: Miner! is a gold mine simulator where your goal is to mine as much gold as possible with your 15 charges of dynamite without blowing your equipment up.

games.name: Miner 2049er
games.overview:
You play the part of Bounty Bob, and it is your mission to explore every inch of an abandoned mine. As you walk over floor sections in the mine, the floor will change color. When all of the floor sections have been changed in color, you can move on to the next, more challenging level. To reach all of the floor sections, you will need to figure out how to get there.

You can jump (be careful not to fall too far though, or you will be squished), climb up and down ladders, and use different transportation devices that can be found on the levels (such as an elevator, slides, a springboard, or a cannon). Wandering around the mine are numerous radioactive creatures which get in Bounty Bob's way. Also scattered throughout the mines are various artifacts left behind; if Bounty Bob collects one of these, the creatures will temporarily become vulnerable. If Bounty Bob runs into one of the creatures in this state the creature will be destroyed, but if he runs into a creature while it is glowing Bounty Bob will be destroyed.

There is a total of ten different levels, and to complete them all you will need quick reflexes as well as to figure out a unique strategy for each level.

games.name: Miner (COMPUTE! Publications)
games.overview:
Miner is a game with some resemblance to Boulder Dash, but also has a unique spin on the genre. You start off at the top of the screen, underneath a building of some sorts. Your goal is to dig through the screen finding gold along the way. Unlike Boulder Dash however, boulders cannot crush you, but you can use them to trap enemies that actually can kill you. Collect as much gold as you can and return it to the building once there is enough gold in the building it's onto the next screen.

Miner was developed by Gus Vakalis and published as a type-in listing in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1991/07 which was an insert in the Compute Magazine.

games.name: Miner (Data-Tronic)
games.overview: Miner is a Boulder Dash clone developed by Øystein Berg and published by Data-Tronic. The year of release is not known. Unlike most Boulder Dash clones on the Commodore 64, this one was built from the ground up, and not made using the Boulder Dash Construction Kit. Berg programmed the game using just green, black, and some white to make it look as if it was done on a monochrome computer such as the Commodore PET.

games.name: Mines of Merlin
games.overview: As published in Ahoy! 1988/06 (Issue #54) this is an enhanced version of Vault of Terror, a text adventure game.

games.name: Mines of Saturn
games.overview: During a routine orbit of Saturn you encounter a radiation storm which forces you into the rings causing you to lose your ships energy. The only solution is to make an emergency landing on the planet's surface which was successful and luckily you landed next to an old abandoned mine full Di-Lithium Crystals. Your mission now is to enter the mine and collect enough crystals to re-fuel your ship and leave Saturn.

games.name: Minesweep
games.overview: A version of Minesweeper that was released both in GO64! 2003/03, and also on GO64! 2004/02. This is game based on the PC desktop game Minesweeper. Try and uncover safe paths, but if you uncover a mine, then you're toast.

games.name: Minesweeper 64
games.overview: Minesweeper 64 is a Minesweeper clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Erik Engdahl and released into the public domain in 1993.

games.name: Minesweeper (Compute!)
games.overview: A Minesweeper clone for the C64 created by Robert B. Cook and published in 1993 in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1993/06.

games.name: Minesweeper (CP Verlag)
games.overview:
A nice version of minesweeper that was published in Magic Disk 64 1995/04.

Minesweeper demands your full concentration: this is about the targeted defusing of bombs!

At the beginning you will see some numbers and boxes on the playing field. The numbers provide information about how many bombs are hidden in the immediate vicinity (i.e. a box!). Now you have to deduce logically where there are bombs and where they are not. Pressing the fire button once (joystick in port # 2) marks a field as a bomb and pressing it twice reveals a field. If you uncover a field and unexpectedly a bomb appears, the game is over.

games.name: Mini Boulder
games.overview: A boulder Dash style game that was part of the "Antics" game pack. Tired of the normal programming work, the Artgames team rummaged through the archive box again and discovered four slightly older, previously unreleased games. Since Mini-Boulder is not only small and compact, but also a lot of fun to play, it was decided to it up to date by reprogramming and to publish it along with Elvin, Chip-War and Dulcedo Cogitations (Sweet thoughts) together in the Antics four pack. Digitized graphics and five harmonious sounds for four times the fun!

games.name: Mini-Dash
games.overview: An updated version of Boulderdash with added caves to explore and loot! Created by Carl Muller and publshed by ZZap!64. “Mini-Dash” introduces new levels in the style of “Boulder Dash.” Players must once again apply clever strategies to overcome obstacles, collect diamonds, and avoid deadly dangers. The new challenges require precise timing and foresight to successfully complete the levels.

games.name: Mini Golf (Capcom)
games.overview: Mini Golf is a breath of fresh air, a slice of "holesome" fun and entertainment for up to four players to get hooked on! Mini Golf is 18 holes of realistic, challenging golf, with all of the frustrations and rewards an individual experiences while playing this unique game.

games.name: Mini Golf (Laing Marketing)
games.overview: The pressure is on - hit the ball around the sand trap, by a water hazard and through the rotating vanes. Par 4, you think incredulously! 18 challenging holes. Each completely different. Use walls to bank around hazards.

versions.label: Miniature Golf (1985)(Data Plane)[cr Somebody Else Inc.]

games.name: Mini-Munch
games.overview: A single-screen pac-man game, possibly intended as a loader-game as the maze never changes and only 2 to 3 ghosts.

games.name: Mini-Putt
games.overview: Mini Putt is a miniature golf game that offers 4 courses, Deluxe, Classic, Traditional and Challenge. Up to 4 players can either play a game or practice any hole on any course. Each course offers its own difficulty level. Deluxe and Challenge have difficult hills and course layouts. The Challenge being the more difficult course. The Classic offers animated bridges and other obstacles. The traditional is your standard miniature golf course which requires well placed bank shots.

games.name: Mini Racers
games.overview: A PETSCII racing game, a day at the speedway.

games.name: Mini-Tris
games.overview: Mini-Tris is a simple single player Tetris clone with simple graphics developed by Waldemar Schott and published by Markt & Technik in 64'er 1990/08.

games.name: Mini-Zork I
games.overview: Mini-Zork has been compared to a Reader's Digest edition of a classic. The Mini-Zork is one of several remakings of Zork from the final years of Infocom. Mini-Zork I had a brief shelf-life in computer shops, in Activision packaging, but it is now best known for its magazine release. In November 1990, a year after Infocom had effectively become defunct, the Mini-Zork was given away with the British Commodore users' magazine "Zzap! 64" no. 67, which is now a collector's item.

games.name: Minima
games.overview: A 2D RPG game intended to be a mini-version of Ultima and part of the 2001 Minigame Competition 2K Category.

games.name: Minima Reloaded
games.overview: Was released as part of the Minigame Competition 2003 - 4K Category.

games.name: Mining
games.overview: A boulder-dash style puzzle, action game published in 64'er Sonderheft 49.

games.name: Minipedes
games.overview:
Inspired by the arcade game Centipede, a garden is in the height of summer but is full of unsavory creatures and a mutant mushroom monster called Minipede. You must blast the Minipede to clear a level as well as the other creatures including spiders, snails and ladybirds for bonus points over 15 levels. You sit at the bottom of the screen where you can move left or right, and forwards a short distance as well as backwards. The Minipede moves across the screen from the top and advances downwards when it reaches one side of the screen. Scattered around the screen in many numbers are mushrooms which can hinder your movements and when the Minipede hits one it changes direction. If you touch any creature then you lose one of four lives.

The C64 version has 14 different creatures while the C16 and VIC 20 have 10.

games.name: Minit Man
games.overview:
The aliens robots have invaded, and it is up to the Minit Man to load and fire 3 warheads to defeat the alien forces.

First, the aliens have destroyed the bridge required to transport missiles to the launch silos, so the Minit Man must use his helicopter to transport bridge construction material and rebuild the damaged structure. While he is doing this, he must use his helicopter's powerful laser to stop the robot forces from reaching the launch computer deep within Earth's defense fortress. If the robots reach the launch computer, it's game over. The player must be careful of enemy attacks, as they only have 5 hits before it's game over.

After building the bridge, he must protect it from alien assault until a missile has been loaded within the silo. After this, the Minit Man must land on the roof of the defense fortress and go by foot to the launch computer. There, he can fire a rocket towards the invading robotic horde. If the Minit Man can fire 3 rockets, the forces of Earth will be victorious.

games.name: Minitron
games.overview:
A stripped down, mini version of Tron, published in Magic Disk 64 1995/05. 

This fast-paced racing game is based on the movie Tron and is set in the distant future. Since the game was developed exclusively for two players, two joysticks must also be connected. With "+" and "-" you can regulate the speed and adapt it to your personal abilities. Only when both players press the joystick button does the game begin.

Each player controls a vehicle that leaves a trace on the race track. You must now be extremely careful not to touch your own trail or that of the opponent. That would mean one point for the opponent. Both players have the option of doubling the speed by holding down the fire button.
If a player has reached nine points, the game starts over. Have fun!

games.name: Minnesota Fats Pool Challenge
games.overview:
Minnesota Fats' Pool Challenge a.k.a. Hustler is an overhead pool table view allowing one or two players to shoot six different configurations of pocket pool, or billiards, for score. The game requires a joystick and key commands to Shoot, break, or bank cue ball shots against an opponent, or the table.

The six play templates are as follows:
1. One player, any ball, any pocket.
2. One player, balls in order.
3. One player, ball in specific pocket.
4. Two player, Score the pockets.
5. Two player, Mini Pool.
6. Two player,lowest and highest numbered ball.

games.name: Minotax
games.overview: Don your jetpack and we'll shoot our way into the heavily defended fortress. Avoid the guns and make your way past the traps and laser guardians to the heart of the citadel and take out the generators. It is a bit of a maze in there. Take out every brick in the protective walls and they will fall. We can be victorious.

games.name: Misfortune
games.overview: A scrolling screen platformer by Bad Bytes (Mathew Cox, Dwayne J. Bakewell, Matthew McHugo & Kellie) New and released in 1999 in Loadstar #185, Loadstar #248, and also in Reset #10 Mix-i-Disk. In this game you will find yourself jumping for keys in a side-scrolling winter wonderland. A jump and shoot game from Bad Bytes, an Australian coding group. There are 5 worlds to explore and each one contains five keys that must be gathered to a chest. You can move your little guy underneath square blocks and bump into them changing color or giving a power up icon. Some will contain keys. You can also find, coins, extra time, point bonuses and 3 different attack powers. If you pass a check point marker it will change colors and you can start there if you die. Remember there is a time limit so you have to hunt and kill fast.

games.name: MISL: Major Indoor Soccer League
games.overview: The official game of the MISL, this game allows you to create an expansion team and build it into a championship franchise. You can trade and create players, modify team rosters, and train players for the season. Team stats are kept for 9 seasons, and the game offers the ability to coach, GM, play or all 3.

versions.label: MISL Major Indoor Soccer League (1987)(Mindscape)[cr Wise]

games.name: Miss All Nude America
games.overview:
Your typical macho game. First enter how many there are in the Jury, then their names. Now you can judge face, boobs, overall appearance
and the computer will calculate the winner based on your ratings... 
 
Miss All Bare America: Every year in the U.S. they elect the Miss All Bare America. You usually see tiny excerpts in cinema or on your video.
But Computer freaks - now your C-64 makes it possible: You and your party-guests are members of the jury to vote who of the 40 prettiest girls will win the com- petition who will be the Miss All Bare America. A disc full of superb graphics showing dream girls you'll love

games.name: Miss Milligan
games.overview:
Miss Milligan is a patience game which is played using two decks of playing cards. According to Peter Arnold, author of Card Games for One, this classic game's enduring popularity is in part due to its amazing tendency to enable complete recovery from seemingly hopeless positions.

Rules:

First, eight cards are dealt in a row; they are bases for eight columns in the game. Any ace that becomes available is put onto the foundations, to be built up by suit. Other cards are built down by alternating color. One card can be moved at a time, although a sequence can also be moved in part or in whole as one unit. When an empty column occurs, only a King or a sequence starting with a King can be placed on it.

When no more moves can be made, a new set of eight cards is dealt, each for every column, whether full or empty. Then the game resumes until all possible moves are exhausted, after which a new set of eight cards is placed. This cycle of dealing new cards and making moves continues until the stock is exhausted.

After the stock has run out, there is no redeal. However, there is special move called either "waiving" or "weaving". The player can pick up a card or a sequence of cards and set it aside (this is the dominant rule; some rule sets state that only one card can be picked up). The card or sequence can later be placed back on to the tableau at any time as long as it can be built legally. Only one card or sequence of cards can be set aside at a time. Computerized solitaire applications that feature this game include a reserve cell for this purpose.

The game ends when no more useful moves can be made. The game is won if all cards are built onto the foundations. 

The C64 version was written by Maurice Jones and published by J & F Publishing in Loadstar #167 in 1998.

games.name: Miss Mind: Ania
games.overview: Miss Mind Ania is a puzzle-board game. The player's task is to guess the sequence of five digits in six attempts. At the top of the screen the player indicates digits from 0 to 9. The results of the trials are shown on the top right side of the screen: full dot (C64 - hearts) is a perfect match, half full dot (C64 - question mark) means that the digit occurs in a different place.

versions.label: Miss Mind Ania (1992)(ABC Soft)[cr Chromance Coderz]

games.name: Missile Blasta
games.overview: Published in GO64! 2003/01and also in GO64! 2004/03.  You are in deep space, defending your own home planet from the incoming of giant alien nuclear missiles. Blast those to pieces and score 100 points per hit. Avoid contact with missiles, otherwise you lose a shield. Lose all 5 shields, your ship will be destroyed and Earth will be lost.

games.name: Missile Busters
games.overview: A catch it type game. Your planet is under threat by an evil alien race. Therefore it is up to you to collect those missiles into the Missile Compaction Container. The only way to survive is to NOT lose all your lives, otherwise the alien forces have won. The planet will get destroyed and only the Aliens will live.

games.name: Missile Busters II
games.overview: A collect-em-up style game. Your planet is under threat by falling missiles. Therefore it is up to you to collect those missiles into the Missile Compaction Container - again.. The only way to survive is to NOT let the contamination damage counter reach 100% otherwise your planet is doomed. There are various power ups which could be handy or useless. Left + Right arrow objects will expand your container's length, so that collecting missiles is easier. Avoid the bomb power ups, otherwise say bye bye to your home planet. :o)

games.name: Missile Command (CP Verlag)
games.overview:
A Missile-Command clone game created by Jüggisoft and published in Magic Disk 64 1990/11. 

In this variation as well as defending against incoming ICBMs you need to defend the planet from the Romulan Warbirds and other alien ships. As fascinating as the game is, its instructions are simple. There are no cumbersome controls and no superfluous displays, and there is no great storyline either. Since CP-Verlag does not concern me with doing nothing, I will tell you a little bit more about MISSILE-COMMAND.

In the distant future: The extraterrestrials (who else?! In this regard It seems that from the year 2000 a lot is coming towards us earth dwellers...!) one is planning more of an attack on our good old earth. This time our friends have come up with something very special: We are being irradiated! Contrary to their usual practice, this time we don't have to shoot our way through countless waves of attack and bomber formations and - instead, stop the rays that are inexorably moving towards our mother planet with a gigantic rocket launcher.

In any case, it is important to prevent a jet from falling directly on one of the six cities and dissolving them into dust and rubble. It is therefore a matter of firing a rocket into orbit the descending rays. If the rocket explodes a little in front of the beam, the resulting short-term protective screen absorbs the attacker and thus renders him harmless. When all cities are hit and destroyed, the battle is lost!

Every now and then ships of the aliens cross the screen at great heights. If your hands are full, you might want to remember them and send them a missile or two. This not only has a positive effect on your points account, but also testifies to the great, unselfish commitment of your fellow players!

games.name: Missile Command (Interceptor Software)
games.overview: Missile Command is a side view single screen shooter based on the arcade game of the same name where you have to protect six cities on the bottom of the screen, on the planet Eetalamer with a missile base between the cities. The enemy are sending I.G.L. Missiles which move from the top of the screen downwards, leaving behind a trail and you must stop them hitting the cities. You fire a limited amount of missiles one at a time and you control a cross-hair to show where the missile should explode. Once the missile explodes it creates a fireball which expands and if a missile hits the fireball it is destroyed. If a city is hit by the enemies missiles then it is destroyed and stays destroyed for the rest of the game. Once all missiles have been destroyed or hit the ground you receive bonus points for any remaining cities and missiles and if any cities left you move to the next level. Planes and satellites occasionally appear on the screen and these can be destroyed for bonus points.

games.name: Missile Defender
games.overview: A Missile Command clone coded entirely in BASIC. Shoot your anti-missile weapon and save the cities from destruction. Published as a type-in game in the book "PCW Games Collection for the Commodore 64".

games.name: Mission-1: Project Volcano
games.overview: You have been selected for this Mission because of your specialist skills in computer operations. The Aim of your Mission is to gain entry to the hidden Command complex, once there you must locate the main computer room and delete the command program by entering the Destruct Code. Intelligence informs us that this code is hidden within the complex.

games.name: Mission 2: Project Gibraltar
games.overview: Enter the secure area on The Rock and discover the secret of the Blue Room. This is the sequel to Mission 1: Project Volcano. Mission 2: Project Gibraltar is a text adventure with some graphics. A Russian agent has infiltrated a nuclear complex on Gibraltar. Your mission is to identify and "remove" the spy.

games.name: Mission A.D.
games.overview: Earth is in trouble once again after minor attacks against our planet and scientists have predicted that there will be one final big attack that will totally destroy us. The scientists have devised a plan called Mission A.D. which will see all countries join their defense systems and give financial aid to the plan. All countries agreed apart from one, Silesia, which sees it's Head of State General Offisrokka condemn the plan as he feels it's a capitalist plan to take over his country. Assassins hired by the General have now been dispatched to the bunker where the plans are being devised and drawn up to kill the scientists.

versions.label: Mission AD (1986)(Odin Computer Graphics)[cr Dynamic Duo]
Mission AD (1986)(Odin Computer Graphics)[cr REM][t +4 REM]
Mission AD (1986)(Odin Computer Graphics)[cr REM][t +4 REM][Docs][#011]
Mission AD (1986)(Odin Computer Graphics)[cr REM][t +4 REM][Docs]

games.name: Mission Asteroid
games.overview:
In this game, you play an astronaut who is asked by Mission Control to send a rocket up to an asteroid and blow it up before it reaches Earth. The trouble is: you will be unable to find the asteroid without a flight plan. This early adventure game is very short, and, in order to accomplish the task, the game requires you to enter one- or two-word commands to perform various actions. The game may be saved to a floppy disk at any point in the game.

Enter the world of computer adventure. Each Sierra On-Line adventure takes several weeks to master providing hours of fascination and intrigue. The player must use their imagination and logic to unlock the mysteries of each adventure. Map skills are a must since our adventure games contain over a hundred full-color computer-generated images which lead you in every direction. So, muster up all your wit, logic and perseverance for this is a Sierra On-Line adventure and a challenge to your ingenuity. An asteroid of overwhelming proportions is on a collision course with the planet Earth. As an astronaut, it is your duty and hazardous adventure to rocket to the asteroid and alter its course. But, there is no time to waste! If procedures and instructions are not followed precisely, disaster is eminent.

games.name: Mission Egg
games.overview:
A whimsical, ova themed collect'em up game published in Magic Disk 64 1988/06. 

It's the year 2020. After a nuclear war, the earth was devastated. But the surviving people have already adjusted to their new way of life. Actually, life goes on just as it did 33 years ago, but there are exceptions.

There are z. B. Giant chickens, which of course also lay giant eggs. The giant chickens just don't want to hatch their own eggs themselves. As a chicken farmer, you only have one option:

You have to take matters into your own hands. Fortunately, in this warm climate, which prevails all over the world, a small step (FIRE BUTTON) is enough for you to go against the giant eggs to bring the chicks to hatch.

However, these actions are not entirely safe, especially since there are radiation-contaminated clouds everywhere, which our chicken farmer PIT has to cleverly avoid. Any contact with the shadow of the clouds and the clouds themselves means death for PIT. Only the cloud that PIT constantly chases is harmless. Because this cloud is enriched with cosmic rays and only leads to a small change of location.
Fortunately, PIT can jump too. After pressing the SPACE key, PIT can break free from any predicament with one jump. But there the jumps at them
are limited to each level, you should divide the jumps well. 

The aim of the game is to free all chicks from their eggs and then to kick them off the screen with one last kick. If the chick and cloud collide while being ejected, the radioactive force of the cloud is discharged and the chick explodes. Since this effect also earns points and can also destroy dicey clouds that have come close, you should make use of this effect. In all the pictures there are small coins that can be picked up when PIT approaches them horizontally. These coins give bonus points when you reach a new level. Have fun!

games.name: Mission Elevator
games.overview: A bomb has been set by terrorists to blow up a sky-scraping hotel in which the FBI’s Central Intelligence Unit is located, and you must diffuse it. Reaching the room itself is no easy task, as the hotel is split into segments of 8 floors, and you can’t move onto the next one without the emergency key, which the porter has hold of – he must be located. Each of these has one eighth of the secret stop code, and these must be entered in order to finally diffuse the bomb. Secrets can be gleaned from the opposing hijackers, and from the barman. In some cases furniture can be used to your advantage. The whole game is similar to Impossible Mission, requiring lots of logic, puzzle-solving and structured thought.

games.name: Mission Genocide
games.overview: Your mission is to fly over the Bad Star Empire in your star fighter and destroy as much of their world as you can in response to them attacking and devastating your planet CRYS-CIT. The more damage you inflict on their fighters and installations means the less chance they will attack again and finally destroy your planet.

games.name: Mission II
games.overview: The security of the universe is in danger! Some evils placed several bombs in different systems. It's your task is to collect all the bombs and to make them inactive. You have only limited time until the bombs will explode!  Another one with shifty gravity. Watch those walls... too late... BOOM! Published in 64'er 1990/11, 64'er Sonderheft 73, 64'er 1998/08, SYS PD Diskett#49 (1994).

versions.label: Mission II (1990)(Markt & Technik)[cr Austrian Cracking Crew]

games.name: Mission Impossibubble
games.overview: The trickiest isometric maze this side of Armageddon comes your way. Search and rescue missions have never been so bizarre! Released in Commodore Format 1992/01 (Issue #16).

games.name: Mission Monday
games.overview:
A horizontally scrolling shooter.  Jump mines and obstacles in your armed jeep. Take out the baddies, bouncing balls, tanks and other foes. Set in the Vietnam war, Mission Monday\Tan is a game that takes place right in the middle of the conflict. The protagonist is a brave Sergeant Tan who has the important mission of delivering an urgent and very secret order to an outpost located in the middle of the jungle where there is a group of isolated soldiers. The enemy forces have surrounded the area and therefore our hero will need to do authentic stunts to complete the mission. Jump the mines that have been arrayed against you, destroy tanks, dodge traps and fight the soldiers and you will be able to complete Mission Monday. 

Published in Italy under the name Tan in various publications including Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - big 100 (1987), Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - maxi commodore (1988),  Special Games n.14 (giugno 1988) and Super C64 e C128 n.23 (maggio 1988).

games.name: Mission Nada
games.overview:
Published in Magic Disk 64 1992/04. 

We regret . . .  were the last words transmitted by the scouts who passed through the B-screens in the course of "MISSION NADA". So we are unable to tell you anything more that will prepare you for this mission. Since you have already shown courage in the face of death, by entering the kiosk and depositing 9.80 DM from the depths of your pants pockets and fearlessly placed the monies on the dark sales counter you are also free to enjoy the fulfillment of this task. So step in, and with your space glider on a journey into the unknown, fare well. We will not hold you back, but wish that if the Devil chases you, you will be faster than his trident.

games.name: Mission Omega
games.overview:
AKA - Mission Ω
Omega is the codename for a mysterious alien craft which has appeared in space, armed with potentially destructive missiles. Your task is to reach it, and then disable its four reactors and escape within a hour - this way it can be explored, and its technology exploited, without it firing a missile or falling into enemy hands.

You do this by guiding a robot droid through the corridors and rooms which make up the ship. You control the game using an icon system, and your first task is to configure the robot with the weapons and power supply you feel will be the most effective. Rather than individually directing each move, you can use the inbuilt map to plot a course for the robot.

games.name: Mission on Thunderhead
games.overview:
From the author of Maxwell Manor, Mission on Thunderhead is an action game with a science-fiction theme.

Thunderhead is a once-desolate planet now teeming with life, thanks to the hated Eternals. They have set up an underground complex, which is their main power base.

The game is split into two parts - Operation Tempest and The Final Appeal. In Operation Tempest you must find and activate the device needed to destroy the planet. In The Final Appeal you must find the items which will allow you to appeal the charges the Eternals hit you with.

Gameplay involves jumping and shooting - the player must collect the items which allow you to defeat monsters. There are also mazelike sections. Weapon power-ups and reloads can be found, as can extra lives. The game has 10 preset levels, and a seed number to allow over 1000 variations of play.

games.name: Mission X
games.overview: A text adventure game written using AdventureWriter/Quill. Was also released as part of the "5 Adventures" game pack., sold at computer fairs and distributed through mailing lists, making them amongst the rarest of all C64 releases. You are taken by aliens to a distant planet simulated to look like an English village and your mission is to return to Earth.

games.name: Mission X-14
games.overview: A graphically enhanced German text adventure game. A mad professor develops X-14 and threatens the world, take control of an agent who has to find out the secret of X-14, steal it, if possible and get your agent to safety.

games.name: Mission X-2
games.overview: A platforming game published in 64'er Sonderheft 37. The starbank of Astra, the richest deposit of precious gems and metals in the entire galaxy has always been considered an impregnable fortress, thanks to the highly sophisticated electronic alarm systems that control a myriad of unstoppable cyber guards. But for those charged with Mission X-2, the enterprise of robbing the big bank represents a goal and a challenge of great prestige. For this reason he has decided to challenge the impenetrability of the complex. While getting into it was a fairly easy feat, our hero will now have to contend with the infamous robotic hordes. The myriads of traps capable of incinerating anything face the your team. If you are skilled, you will be able to interfere in the control of the guardians from the numerous terminals or receive useful information to open the way to wealth and fame.

games.name: Missioncode CX-13
games.overview:
Published in Compute mit 1987/03 and in Ballerspiele-Sammlung. 
Shooting whatever it takes, that's the motto of this program. Their secret mission is to destroy the enemy base.

games.name: Missione Odessa
games.overview:
A Jackson Soft text adventure in Italian about finding and stopping the Nazi "rat-lines" of escape from Germany to Argentina and Brazil following World War II. The name ODESSA is an acronym for the German phrase "Organization der ehemaligen SS-Angehörigen", which translates as "Organization of Former Members of the SS". 
 
An English translation was released in 2016 by the same author.

games.name: Misty Island
games.overview:
Misty Island is a standard text adventure for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Dorothy Millard and published by The Adventure Workshop in 1994.

Story:

You know too much, and have been unceremoniously dumped semiconscious on a remote misty island, with no food, to die. Of course this doesn't appeal to you, dying, that is!

Can you find a way to survive this nightmare, and even escape back to civilization?

In your semiconscious state, you hear spies whispering about "hiding the evidence". The men leave you to regain consciousness. Now it's up to you.

games.name: Mit Jeans und Hellebarde
alt_names: Mit Jeans & Hellebarde: Vor dem Sturm
games.overview: A text adventure in German language. The plot follows a man from today who suddenly finds himself in medieval times. The player has to solve puzzles by typing in commands with the keyboard.

versions.label: Mit Jeans & Hellebarde Vor dem Sturm (1988)(Electronic Design)(de)

games.name: Moby Dick
games.overview: Moby Dick is a side view single screen game where you control a boat on the sea, that moves from the left to the right of the screen on top of the water constantly, but you can speed it up or slow it down. The idea of the game is to drop depth charges two at a time, to blow up submarines that move across the screen from right to left below. A helicopter also moves across the screen above from left to right and can be shot with a missile, but the helicopter will drop bombs to hit you. As you drop the depth charges, you must be aware of a whale swimming across the screen and you cannot hit it or a green boat appears and rams you losing you one of five lives. Getting hit by a helicopter bomb loses you a life but if you hit the helicopter then the pilot parachutes downwards and if you catch him then you get bonus points. This was released in North America as part of 3 Arcade Games - Book 1 from Cymbal Software, Inc.

games.name: Model Builder
games.overview: Create your model cars, give them Engines, transmissions and fuel systems and then take them out on the track for speed and handling trials.

versions.label: Model Builder (1985)(Creative Sparks)[cr The Southern Cross]

games.name: Modem Wars
games.overview: One or two player real-time strategy game where you control armies of Infantry, Cavalry, Artillery, and Spies searching for your opponent's Command Center. Modem required for second player.

games.name: Modulus
games.overview:
The war against the Xarvi is turning to term; the last offensive unleashed by horrifying insects bent the shaky defense
the X-25 galactic quadrant; many human settlements They fell into the hands of the invaders.

The higher council has decreed an immediate counteroffensive to prevent the Xarvi from arriving directly to the central star group, so as to safeguard freedom throughout the galaxy; but Counteroffensive will not take place if the station
Xarva main space located at the center of the sector galactic X-25 will not be disabled until this builds the network of conquest, the last Found in the Neutron War.

That's why a secret agent must infiltrate in the spatial base, identify all codes of access and penetrate the control room, where it can ably disable the computer that Controls the Xarva offensive.

A mass attack would be of no use, Space station is defended by the most aggressive Xarva garrison that uses the fast
Asgerat combatcruit cruisers, capable of Reduce to pieces the largest stellar fleet of the The Confederation of Free Humans. This is why one and A single agent can infiltrate between Xarve files, penetrate the galactic sector X-25 and reach the space station. A complicated lift system allows you to reach the various sections of the Station.

games.name: Moebius
games.overview: Moebius is a side scrolling shoot 'em up. It's set on a far away planet where the player takes control of Moebius, a space mercenary that has to battle the forces of The Controller, the ruler of the empire. The player can move Moebius left and right while shooting the various creatures and robots that appear before they crash into him. Each level is a different planet and the aim is to reach a transporter that takes Moebius to the next planet. Every planet has its own inhabitants that has to be fought. After a few levels the player will get access to a jetpack and later a hovercar. Using these cost fuel and when fuel is out they will explode. Fuel is automatically recharged when walking on the ground.

games.name: Moebius: The Orb of Celestial Harmony
games.overview: Khantun is traditionally a peaceful land, with no army or wars. Former leader Kaimen has turned to using his powers for evil, and the land has not withstood his aggression. The Holy Ones have been kidnapped, the land instead ruled by an evil group of monks. It is down to the player to vanquish Kaimen and restore the path of righteousness. The game combines top-viewed role playing elements with combat action. The player explores the lands, but when encountering unfriendly people the player must fight, using swords or martial arts moves, as well as long-range missiles and magical powers.

versions.label: Moebius The Orb of Celestial Harmony (1987)(Origin Systems)

games.name: Mole Attack
games.overview: This was a Japanese MAX cartridge release. These could be played on the C64 and were occasionally repackaged with a "slap-on" sticker and sold in Europe. Mole Attack is one of the earliest computerized Whac-a-Mole variants. Gameplay should be clear: Moles randomly pop out of several holes (arranged in a 3x3 grid), and you can hit them using the right keyboard key (one for each hole). The sooner you hit the mole's head, the more points you get -- but if you hit the mole's buttocks (yes, them buggers sometimes pop up that way), you lose points. After 60 seconds, the game ends and your score is shown.

games.name: Molecule Man
games.overview: Molecule Man is trapped inside a radioactive maze of 256 screens, and it's your job to get him out. To do this you must collect 16 circuits which are located at extreme points of the levels. You must regularly consume radiation tablets to fend off certain poisoning, and your initial supply of 20 is totally inadequate. Fortunately, there are coins dotted around the levels, as well as ant-radiation tablet vending machines at which you can buy them. Coins can also be used to buy more time, or to blow up obstacles which make some sections difficult or impossible to access. Viewed isometrically, the screen designs are intentionally surreal, each taking on an unlikely distorted real-world theme. If you find the initial level layouts too easy, too hard or too dull, you can design a new set with the bundled maze editor.

games.name: Mondial Simulation 1990
games.overview: A football\soccer simulation with arcade elements featuring the 1990 World Cup event.

games.name: Mondu's Fight Palace
games.overview: Tongue of the Fatman is an eclectic fighting game. Choose from different alien races (including Human) with different abilities and fighting styles, purchase weapons and devices, and fight your way through multiple opponents to face the Fatman. Some of the features include being able to place wagers on the outcome of the fight, and the phenomenon of a special move being less powerful the more you use it to balance gameplay. Two-player, head-to-head combat is supported.

games.name: Monkey Magic
games.overview: Based on the original television series that ran from 1978 to 1980, the player controls Monkey as he makes his way through four levels and rescue the princess from the evil dragon. In the first level, the player rides a cloud, and must use lightning bolts to destroy three waves of flying creatures. In the second level, the player must collect all the fruit while avoiding or jumping over creatures. Vines and ladders must be navigated in order to get some fruit. The third level has the player navigating a steep cliff. Four birds drop rocks onto the path, causing it to crack. The player must jump over these cracks. Finally, in the last level, the player must defeat the dragon by throwing spears at it, while avoiding its fire.

games.name: Monkey Match
games.overview: Monkey Match is a 2 player only memory game. It was developed by Anthony Rose and published in Loadstar #169.

games.name: Monolith Tank
games.overview: A vertically scrolling Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit based game where you and your buddy take on jets, other tanks and fortified positions while avoiding or destroying tank traps that block the way and limit maneuverability. One or two can play and it supports simultaneous 2 player, which is a real blast. Published in ECP's "War Games Pak" compilation.

games.name: Monopole
games.overview: Just like Monopoly except without the Y and the trademark. You can optionally choose to use the Auction rule.

games.name: Monopoly (HC Mein Home-Computer)
games.overview:
German version of Monopoly, published by HC - Mein Home-Computer 1984/07. No definite name, called "Quadropoly" in the magazine, info in game calls itself Monopoly. The program is based on the well-known board game Monopoly, but adds a few fields and differs from it in some features. It uses German streets instead of the US ones in the Milton Bradley version. The street group Badstrasse, Turmstrasse is extended by the Lindenstrasse and the street group Parkstrasse, Schloßallee by the Feldschmiede. There are three control panels; the taxes to the state have been halved (income tax is 2000 marks). Another work is the municipal utility. The factor for owning all three works is 200. This results in a maximum rent of 2000 marks in total.
The Commodore 64 conjures up a game board on the screen and simulates it.  The event and community fields have been merged. 22 different events are possible. When you go to prison, you have the opportunity to get out with a double. You can go into debt up to a limit of 40,000 marks.

games.name: Monopoly (Leisure Genius)
games.overview:
This version of the classic board game supports several graphic formats and offers some different options. From 2 to 8 players can play the game, and they can all be computer players if you wish. This allows you to just sit back and watch as the computer takes over. You can choose to play a short game with a specified time limit, or a standard game, and there is a save game feature.
