There has been a crime and it's up to Topper to find the clues to apprehend the criminal from seven suspects and send him to jail within a time limit. The area is a collection of rooms on four levels connected by corridors and a lift system. The rooms are platforms games with a number of safes which may or not contain a clue about the crime. Collect them all until you have eight clues. One of the safes also contains a key to the jail. In the rooms are baddies and obstacles which need avoiding as a touch decreases part of your energy bar but can be replenished by visiting the police station. Lose your energy and it's game over.

The lift system consists of baskets moving up and down all the way down to the bottom level and up to the top level. Miss jumping into a basket and you fall into the boiler at the bottom and it's game over. Once you have collected the eight clues you can go to the courthouse where you are given a random riddle and using your clues you must answer it, get it right and you can take the criminal to jail.

The platform rooms are shown on one screen and the corridor sections are flick screen and viewed from the side. A joystick is used to control Topper.

games.name: Topsy-Turvy
games.overview: The player's task is to reach the bomb and return to the exit, which will appear after it is activated. Activating the bomb converts all enemy creatures into points to be collected. While completing the task, avoid contact between the balloon and moving and stationary elements, as well as lasers. An additional difficulty is the passing of time. Created by Heino Görtz and published in Happy Computer 1987/09.

games.name: Torchbearer
games.overview: Years ago, Talis Valutheart, a powerful and evil wizard, stole the Torch of Truth and hit it somewhere within the many sanctuaries and dungeons of Pastoria. With the people thus blinded, Vaultheart began to take the land. The time has ocme for a new hero to take it back! Will you accept the challenge? The Kingdom of Pastoria is a large island with many smaller islands surrounding. You will explore many of them on your quest for the lost Torch. Although you start as a common citizen, you are far from common. You possess the last of the mysterious luckstones! Study magic, increase your fighting strength and speak with the townspeople. All this will help you on your quest. Torchbearer is a challenging graphic adventure game.

games.name: Tornado
games.overview: Tornado is a simple horizontal scrolling shooter developed by Christian Gubert, and published by Multisoft in 1985.

games.name: Torpedo (Susie Software)
games.overview: A submarine battle simulation.

games.name: Torquest
games.overview: You are Maithros. You were found dying, weeks ago, by an old, mystic called Mitherful. He used his reviving magics to heal you. In return for his help he asks you to join the monks.

games.name: Total Eclipse
games.overview:
The game backstory as explained in the manual is that an evil Ancient Egyptian priest has put a curse on a massive pyramid dedicated to the Sun God, Ra. Any object obstructing Ra's shrine from the Sun would be destroyed. The protagonist is an unnamed archeologist who learns that October 26, 1930, a total eclipse will obstruct the sun above Cairo, and the protagonist realized that the curse will cause the Moon to explode, devastating Earth with its debris. The protagonist then decides to travel to that pyramid and destroy the shrine to Ra, preventing the curse/prophecy.

The game starts with the protagonist having just arrived with a biplane parked outside the pyramid he is about to enter, two hours before the eclipse. The player has to enter and explore the pyramid, avoid traps, trigger and activate puzzles and navigate through maze-like rooms. Causes of death include dehydration, and heart attack caused by various hazards such as falling off ledges, getting crushed by falling stones and taking hits from poison darts. Throughout the maze the player can discover treasure to accumulate the score, and also ankhs that serve as keys to locked doors.

games.name: Total Eclipse II: The Sphinx Jinx
games.overview:
Commodore Format 1992/03 (Issue #18). Total Eclipse 2: The Sphinx Jinx a reworking of Total Eclipse sharing many of the same locations, using the Freescape system and vector graphics. To eliminate an ancient curse the player must find 12 pieces of the sphinx within two hours, hidden in the underground passages beneath the pyramid. Except of numerous puzzles the player will face mummies, poisoned darts or heat exhaustion caused by limited access to the water supply. No objects may be collected, although encountered gold bars can significantly enlarge the assets.
also including an A2 colour poster

games.name: Total Recall
games.overview:
Based on the movie of the same name, Total Recall puts you in charge of Douglas Quaid, who must find a way to Mars in order to find the answers to his two questions: why is he being hunted, and who is hunting him. In order to do this, Quaid must go through level after level of beating up bad guys that get in his way.

Some of the levels differ in gameplay, and range between action and driving scenes. The action scenes mainly require you to collect some items before leaving the level. You have only one chance to complete the current level, which means that if your energy is lost, the game ends. Energy is lost if you are attacked by an obstacle, or if you are shot at by an enemy. You can gain more energy by either collecting some pills or a heart, depending on the platform.

games.name: Touchdown Football
games.overview: A very capable football simulation, given the year and technology. Call the plays, then run them using the keyboard or joystick. Digitized voices enhance the game, including the crowd, calling the numbers, and referee's calls.

games.name: Tough Guys
games.overview: Fight your way around the world, and face the toughest guys! 1 or 2 Players simultaneously. Published in Golden Disk 64 1991/02, Golden Disk 64 - Gold Edition. Compete against the computer or a second man as a karate fighter. Defeat your opponents with skill and skill. A mistake would be unforgivable for your future career.

versions.label: Tough Guys (1991)(CP Verlag)[cr Austrian Cracking Crew]

games.name: Tough Guyz
games.overview:
A SEUCK based shooter created by Henk Nieborg and published in 1991. It has the feel of Commando about it. You must break through the hostile landscape and rescue your mates. Two players may play cooperatively.  
 
This game, despite what some incorrect spelling on some media might lead you to believe was never released by CP Verlag. That was a version of the Tough Guys fighting game, not a this shooter.

games.name: Tour de Europe
games.overview: An avoid-it style game from the Italian publisher, LVC. The game was released in 1986. Run across the screen, avoiding all the items (like teapots, wrenches, pots, scissors, spiders, glasses and even a thermos!) falling from the sky and pick up the bags and return them to your side of the screen to gain points. When you get enough bags across you proceed to a new country and background. Make your way across the continent on your tour de Europe.

games.name: Tour de France (Activision)
games.overview:
Tour De France allows you and seven other players the chance to ride in one of the Worlds toughest cycling races. You must ride over various stages as fast as you can, and the fastest time wins. Players don't actually race anyone on screen, each rider takes it in turn to ride a stage solo (one player is just about your time with no computer riders). Before you ride you can decide whether to actually compete in the race or practise. In practise you can actually ride the whole course, ride various stages or one stage. In competition mode you have the same options as practise, whole course, various stages or one stage. Each competitor then enters their name and chooses a country.

The game itself is viewed from the side at a high elevated angles with a small part of the stage shown on the screen. As the rider reaches the end of the screen it scrolls to show a new part of the course. To control the bike you waggle the joystick left to right at a steady pace, to turn you have to hold down the fire button and move left or right. You also have a high or low gear which you change by moving up or down. You must follow the road as you will fall off the bike if you touch the sides losing valuable seconds. A timer appears on each screen and one second is equivalent to one minute. A joystick or keyboard is used to control your rider.

games.name: Tournament Golf
games.overview: Tee off with Tournament Golf, a challenging new computer game from Avalon Hill Microcomputer Games. Loaded with excitement from the amateur to the pro levels. Features 2 complete 18 hole courses with fairways, greens, traps and gophers. A driving range and a putting green for practice and a secret room in the bunker where we can have our raves. All the challenges and frustrations of the sport of golf, all experienced from the comfort of your computer chair.

games.name: Tournament Tennis
games.overview: Anyone for a game of tennis? The game Match Point is a tennis simulation and can be played either against the computer or against another player. As in Wimbledon, here you also play with the real tennis rules. If you are less sportive and rather lean back in your armchair and watch a match, you will also get your money's worth with the good-looking demo mode.

games.name: Tower Commando
games.overview: A shooter created by Bombjack Ltd. on the foundation of the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit made by Chris Yates. The goal is to make it to the top of the tower.

games.name: Tower of Despair
games.overview: Malmor, the Demonlord of Darkness has attempted to overthrow the land of Aelandor many times from the Tower of Despair but many times he has been defeated. In his last defeat, Malmor was sent to the Planes of Limbo by the Council of Wizards thus the believe this was the last time he would rise. But alas no, Malmor has found the artifact, The Ring of Skulls and escaped Limbo and returned to his tower. To make matters worse he has summoned a Hellgaunt to be his servant. This will surely be the last the people of Aelandor can fight and defeat the Demonlord of Darkness.

games.name: Tower Toppler
games.overview:
You play a small green guy who needs to blow up eight towers, because their presence is somehow poisoning the water of planets which could potentially be ideal colonies. Unfortunately you need to get to the top of these towers to blow them up.

You make your way up to the top of the tower via walkways around the outside of the towers. You need to jump over, kick, and run from various enemies in your journey to the top. Most vertical movement is achieved by jumping onto moving ledges at the right moment.

The game was considered revolutionary in its time for its graphic technique. As the main character walked around the outside of the tower, the character was fixed in the middle of the screen while the tower itself rotated. This gave it a pseudo-3D effect.

Towers are linked together via a voyage through the sea in your trusty MK.7 submarine. This plays out as a side-scrolling collect-'em-up in which bonus points can be obtained.

games.name: Toy Bizarre
games.overview:
As a worker at a toy store, you must stop the toy robots from taking over the store, before they take over you. Stop the valves that are getting these toys released in order to control where they land on the floor. Make sure you are ready for those safety checks, turn off the valves before you are hit by hefty Hilda. Stop the toys by jumping over them, or by stunning them. Once you finish doing this, next hour, things start up again.

The game is essentially a clone of the original Mario Bros with different graphics.

games.name: Toyballs
games.overview: A brain - puzzle game developed by ABC Development and published in Magic Disk 64 1992/02.

games.name: Trac Troopa
games.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter from Richard Bayliss and Jon Williams and released in 2004 and published in Commodore Free #070.

games.name: Track & Field
games.overview:
Track & Field is a sports game that allows the player to have an experience based around the Summer Olympic Games. Events include the 100 meter dash, the hammer throw, the javelin throw, the long jump, the high jump and the 110 meter hurdles.

If the player wants to go to the next event or round then they will have to qualify, by beating increasingly difficult maximum times or minimum distances.

games.name: Track Suit Manager
games.overview: Tracksuit Manager varied the conventional Football Manager game style in a number of ways. You take charge of an international team aiming to qualify for and then play in the European Championships and World Cup. This means there is no transfer market, just a pool of 100 eligible players from which a squad of 22 is selected. You can view reports on each player's ability and form at any stage of the squad and team selection process. You can arrange friendly matches to try out players and ensure that the squad plays together as much as possible.

games.name: Tracker
games.overview:
Tracker is a mouse-controlled vector-graphics 3D strategy game depicting an ultra-violent TV show of the future. As a contestant, the player's mission is to be the first to ever complete it successfully. The task involves commanding a fleet of Skimmers charged with destroying various groups of combat vehicles, including Cycloids, Scouts and Defenders. Short and long-range scanners are available to aid in this.

The game takes place in a maze world containing a number of distinct sectors, each of which has its own type of enemy present. The Communication Centre powers the Cycloids, and are protected by the Defenders. Once these are taken out, the Centerpoint Sector must be destroyed to complete the level.

games.name: Traffic
games.overview: Traffic is a simple game where the player has to guide cars, motorbikes and buses through busy London streets by changing the traffic lights from red to green. The objective in order to advance to the next level is to get a preset number of vehicles through the screen, although it does not matter which exit you direct them through. Cars continue to queue off the edges of the screen (with numbers next to them if there are queued cars beyond your vision) and if the queue reach more than five cars, it's game over. A warning sound is given when five cars are queued; you must hope there are not also queues on surrounding roads. Cars always stay on their side of the road, and collisions are not possible.

games.name: Traffic Jam (Island Software)
games.overview: Traffic Jam is a 1983 Board Game for commodore 64, developed and published by Island Software.

games.name: Traffic Jam (RUN)
games.overview: Traffic Jam is an "avoid-it" style game in which your goal is to cross the road from the bottom of the screen to the top in order to get to your house, while avoiding cars and other obstacles. The game was developed by Jeffrey D. Panicki and published in ReRun 1990/01-02. ITS FRIDAY. FIVE O'CLOCK. The heaviest traffic of the week, and you have to walk home, crossing seven lanes of speeding cars as you go. If that weren't enough, your dinner is cooking in the oven and you've got only 40 seconds before it burns up. Another day in the big city. Aarrgghh! That's the scenario for Traffic Jam, a fast-paced arcade-style game

games.name: TrailBlazer
games.overview:
An imaginative action game in which you must guide a ball-shaped craft through a succession of levels. These have a patchwork-quilt type display, with holes to avoid, and squares of various colors, which affect the craft's speed, both within its power potential and into warp, as well as a control-reverser and lots of holes. You can jump and thus avoid these holes, although you have a limited number of them for each level, and it's possible to adjust the speed through joystick or keyboard control. You also face a time limit on each of the levels, although your time is boosted every time you complete one.

Released as part of Commodore Zone Issue #15 / released in the US by Mindscape / part of the "Mega Pack"

games.name: Train Dispatcher
games.overview: Adapted for home computers by designers of systems for major railroads. Train Dispatcher faithfully simulates operations in a railroad traffic control center. In an accelerated 8 hour shift you must move up to 12 trains in both directions through a 150 mile territory - throwing switches and clearing signals to keep the trains on schedule.

games.name: Train Robbers
games.overview:
After successfully being a train robber, Cactus Pete now has a $4000 bounty on his head. You play as Pete as you attempt to rob more locomotives by riding your horse along side and attempting to grab onto a ladder. The game is viewed from the side at a elevated angle as you ride your horse along side the train, and you can speed up or slow down but be careful of any cactus alongside the track which will make you fall of the horse. Push your horse for too long and a timer represented as your horses energy will slowly decrease until it gets to empty and your horse collapses. 

Once you have got onto the ladder you can climb onto the roof of the cars. As you move from right to left you have to navigate the gaps between cars as well as ducking if a tunnel approaches. Once you reach the last car you can drop into it and attempt to find two keys for the safe while avoiding the guard dogs. Touching one loses one of three lives. When you have your loot you need to get back on the roof to get to the front of the train to get back on your waiting horse. The next train awaits. Another player can play and you both take it in turns when the other player loses a life.

games.name: Trains (Spinnaker)
games.overview:
Trains is a top-down management game set in the steam-powered train era. Players control a train to transport goods between stations, loading raw materials at one station and delivering them to industries in need. The goal is to earn money by making deliveries quickly, with extra profits for meeting urgent demands. The game displays industry supply levels on-screen, guiding players on where to deliver goods next.

The train can only move forward and backward along the tracks, with direction changes happening at switches. Each action consumes coal, which must be replenished at coal yards, with penalties for running out. The game deducts money for payroll every few minutes and imposes fines for crashes. Each level features a unique track layout across various terrains, and completing deliveries builds a new track to progress to the next level.

games.name: Trains (Sportscene Specialist Press)
games.overview: The object of this game by Clive Emberey and published in Your 64 No.05 1984/12-1985/01 is to operate the points of a railway network. You have to keep an increasing number of trains on the move without any of them derailing or colliding. As an added problem, some of the points will (of course) fail and close themselves down for repairs. Trains is a game calling for both strategy and fast reactions.

games.name: Trajectory
games.overview: Trajectory is a vertically scrolling shooter for one or two players (co-op)  developed by Richard Hawkins using Chris Yates' SEUCK. It was released to the public domain in 1988.

games.name: Tran
games.overview: A game by Steve Collins of Herobotix and Badlands fame. The unreleased game is based around a sideways space scroller in the mold of Defender, Uridium, Parallax and R-type, with the usual arsenal of weapon upgrades. The aim is to simply blast enemy crafts and collect orbs. When enough are collected, you are able to land and take control of the man on terrain, blasting enemies and saving hostages whom are imprisoned by blowing doors up with bombs. Once all the hostages are saved, its time to find your ship and blast off. When fully specced, you have 6 orbiting droid orbs, each with a lazer cannon. You can have forward and rear double cannons and also sid strafing bazookas.

games.name: Trans-Atlantic Balloon Challenge: The Game
games.overview: In 1987 billionaire and entrepreneur Richard Branson attempted to cross the Atlantic Ocean in a hot air balloon. In the game you have been challenged to a race across the ocean in a hot air balloon with the winner the first to cross the Atlantic Ocean. You can play against a friend or the computer but instead of controlling the balloon you control an eagle with laser sights who controls the balloon. It must defend it as well from the other competitors eagle or a biplane dropping various objects on the balloon. Children also float around carried by balloons and points can be gained for touching them or points lost for killing them.

versions.label: Trans Atlantic Balloon Challenge (1987)(Virgin)[cr Cleveland Cracking Service]

games.name: Trans World
games.overview:
Transworld is a business simulation where you play a young entrepreneur in the carrying business. You start off with a capital of 50.000 DM and a small firm in Frankfurt am Main with the goal of building a business empire.

Apart from managing the delivery of a variety of goods (ranging from oil to food and vehicles), you can also try to increase your wealth by operating at the stock exchange or evading taxes. There are also several other aspects to consider: Too much work will increase your stress level, and if you do not take enough vacations, you will fall ill with corresponding negative effects on your enterprise. Furthermore, the game evaluates your play in three categories (success in business, prestige and trade relations), and winning the game requires a certain number of points in each category.

games.name: Transector
games.overview: Released as part of the "30 Games" game pack. This is like a reverse Gridrunner crossed with PacMan. You need to collect the dots while Gridrunner-like guns fire at you and you are also avoiding baddies zipping around the screen. Very frenetic, a much faster pace than most "collect-em-up" games of this sort.

games.name: Transformation
games.overview: Transformation is a 1988 logical brain puzzle game for the Commodore 64. The game was developed by Joel Epstein and published in Loadstar #052.

games.name: Translogic
games.overview:
A logic based puzzle game developed by Cream Software and published by CP Verlag in Magic Disk 64 1992/11. In this game a lot of brainpower is required. In addition, you have to prove yourself to be a true joystick acrobat in order to be able to adhere to the really tight time limits.
The aim of the game is to bring order into a completely disorganized ball system. For this reason, the screen is also split in half. The left side represents the desired side and the right side the actual chaos. With the cursor you can now try to move the balls so that both sides are identical. When this is done, a quick press of the space button is enough to get to the next level.
In addition, the status line at the top of the screen provides constant information on the most important data. Above all, you should keep an eye on the time limit and act accordingly.

games.name: Transmat
games.overview: A game by Toby Hughes (written when he was 13) and with music by Andrew Colin, published in Commodore Computing International v02-12 (May 1984). It is an adventure game which involves the Transmat - a machine similar to the one used by Captain Kirk and his crew to beam up and down, photon lasers, explosives, a long scarf and a sonic screwdriver because why not?

games.name: Transporter
games.overview: Published in Game On 1990/1, this is a 2 Player-Only game for simultaneous play written originally in German with English unofficially added.

games.name: Transputer Man
games.overview: The sequel to Slap N Tickle. Tragic, mutant, genetic freak, Matthew Slim has found the long lost circuit board. Now you must help our hero to find the Transputer of Learning as only this can free him from the nightmare of being the Transputer Man. This game was one of the samples included in the 1988 release of the Shoot 'Em-Up Construction Kit.

games.name: Transylvania
games.overview: Transylvania is an adventure with optional graphics, and a VERB NOUN interface. Two weeks ago, Princess Sabrina suddenly vanished and remained unseen since. King John the Good asks any travellers to help in locating her - you volunteer. As you begin your quest in the dark forests of Transylvania, beware of the evil that lurks. You will encounter strange creatures like a vampire and a goblin, and experience strange things. Most importantly, a werewolf is constantly chasing you, until you find the pistol and bullets necessary to kill it. Remember fellow traveller, take care...

games.name: Transylvanian Tower
games.overview:
Transylvanian Tower is a single player maze game in which the player must explore five levels of Count Kreepie's castle, kill him, and find his stash of loot. The castle has over five hundred different rooms to explore. Some contain items that can be used but the inventory is limited to only three items at any one time, and this includes weapons, so it's wise to collect just what's important. The items/weapons available are: the golden ring, an invisible cloak, a magic apple, a special floor plan, a clove of garlic, a mirror, a knife, a dagger, a sword, a silver cross and your gun - which is limited to 10 shots. If the player is killed at any time on level 2 and beyond, the game is over and they are returned to the start of level one.

Level 1:
This is an exploration level. A floor plan may be obtained at any time by pressing the 'h' key.

Level 2:
On this level the player will encounter bats and objects. Bats are bad things and must be killed. If enough bats are killed the player will be transported to level 3. If insufficient bats are killed the player will be transported to a random room on level 2. There are sealed rooms and it is possible to be transported into one. Fortunately one of the objects encountered is a magic ring that allows the player to move through two walls, so it is advisable to carry this to avoid having to replay the game. The 'h' key can again be used to view the floor plan, but this time it's only available when a bat has been killed.

Levels 3 & 4:
These play as level 2 but all bats must be shot through the heart.

Level 5:
This is where the evil Count Kreepie resides. Only one of the items you come across will kill the count. This, as the game says, "will force you to find all the objects so you can try them out". After killing the count you will receive a map showing where his treasure is, but you must still fight the bats on the way there.

The game can be saved when necessary, but only after thirty minutes of gameplay. Control is by cursor only. Keys 5-8 move the player in the appropriate direction, key 6 rotates the character 90 degrees to the left, so pressing the 6 key twice means you're retracing your steps. Transfer between levels can take up to two minutes because a new maze is generated for each game.

games.name: Trantor: The Last Storm Trooper
games.overview: In this game you play the role of a man who has been stranded on an alien planet after his space ship explodes and you must find pieces of it to rebuild it. The gameplay involves you jumping across platforms and shooting at droids and aliens but also ducking to avoid high flying robots. The game is played from a side scrolling perspective. The baddies come thick and fast and the only way to cope is to keep moving.

versions.label: Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr SoftWar]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr Beastie Boys]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr Pentacle]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr NewMen]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr SCG]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr RSI]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr Ikari]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr TMS]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr Antitrax]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr MHI][t +3 MHI]
Trantor The Last Storm Trooper (1987)(Probe Software)[cr Triton][t +4 Triton]

games.name: Trap
games.overview:
A once peaceful ally is now your enemy and you are tasked to defend your planet against them. In your spacecraft you must fly your craft blasting and avoiding various enemies intent of killing you over 10 levels. Each level is split into three tests and must be completed to move to the next level. The 1st test sees you in space where mines hurtle towards you at various angles and you can either dodge them or shoot them. Get past this test and the next one see's you flying over a valley where various enemies, some even shoot at you, try to destroy you. Once again you must blast or dodge these.

Scattered on this part stand your comrades who need cargo to keep them going so you can drop cargo for bonus points. Watch out as well for your fuel gauge but this can be replenished by bombing fuel dumps. To get to the 3rd test you must destroy a certain amount of enemies, once you destroy your quota you then leave your craft and move on foot once again avoiding and killing aliens. You have to collect orbs which are needed to complete the game but also you can purchase a better ship. Beware of holes in the ground as this will kill you. At any stage if you touch an alien or get shot you lose one of three lives and back to the start of test 1.

Trap is a vertical shoot-em-up as well as a vertical run 'n gun game viewed from above which sees the screen scroll constantly upwards. You use a joystick and keyboard to play the game.

games.name: Trap (COMPUTE!'s Gazette)
games.overview:
A 3D platform style game created by Eric Haines and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988/05 (Issue #59), and also in Best of Gazette 1988 (Disk Issue). In this fast-paced action game for the 64. You enter a strange new universe where your skill and cunning are put to the test. To survive, you must trap a constantly moving sphere before your time runs out — or you trap yourself.  

"Trap" takes you to another universe, another dimension. Trap's world consists of an array of colored blocks hanging in ink-black space, set against a blanket of distant, sparkling stars. 

Two beings inhabit this strange place, each with a geometrical form; a sphere, which continuously bounces from block to block, and a flat square, which lies atop the blocks, blinking patiently. In Trap, you're the blinking square, and your objective is to trap the bouncing sphere and use its kinetic energy for your survival.

games.name: Trap 'Em
games.overview:
Build fences around your opponent without getting hemmed in yourself n this variation of a Tron Light Cycles game for 1 or 2 players. 

Developed by John Rhees and published in the following:

COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1985/01 (Issue #19)

and in the book "COMPUTE!'s Commodore 64 & 128 Collection"

games.name: Trap-Shooting
games.overview: A crosshairs shooting game simulating the shotgun trap-shooting experience.

games.name: Trap Springer
games.overview: Adventure without whip or Fedora in the Great Pyramid and escape with the gold and your life! A text adventure that belongs in a museum by Damian Steele and released in 1993 by The Adventure Workshop.

games.name: Trashman (Creative Software)
games.overview:
This is a Pacman-style maze game in which you control a garbage truck and try to collect all the trash pieces and bring them to the city dump. Collect all the trash pieces to advance to the next level.

While collecting the trash pieces you must avoid the enemies, which kind of look like birds, maybe like you would find at the dump. 

There are 6 'trash can' power ups per level that allow you to catch the enemies for more points. (Just like how eating a power pill will allow you to eat the ghosts in Pacman).

The game maze features wrap-arounds both at the sides and top to bottom.

games.name: Trashman (New Generation)
games.overview:
While few young people aspire to the role of a Dustman, New Generation Software felt they would enjoy pretending to be one in this innovative arcade game.

Each section presents you with a road of houses, drawn from forced-perspective 3D, with flick-scrolling as you move up the road. Each house's dustbin must be collected, emptied and replaced within the time limit, which is indicated by the Bonus timer at the top of the screen. If this reaches zero, you receive the first of 3 warnings - a third sees you out of a job.

Setting foot on the grass causes the bonus to drop more quickly, and there are additional hazards to avoid, including the local cars, which appear to be driven by maniacs, and cyclists and barking dogs, which can both injure you and cause your movement to slow. Once all the bins have been emptied walking up to the top of the street will complete the level.

games.name: Traverse
games.overview:
An action collect-em-up game created by Tony Brantner and published in RUN 1992/05-06 magazine. This action game will drive you crazy in minutes and keep you entertained for hours. Traverse combines features of Pac-Man and Pinball, with unique twists of its own. Like Pac-Man, it's a travel-the-path-and-eat-the-dots game, each level being a maze with dots along the paths. Unlike Pac-Man, however, you don't direct the ball with traditional joystick commands. Instead, your joystick controls yellow flippers at each intersection of the maze.  Press the fire button to start, then guide the ball across all of the dots, making them disappear. Pressing your joystick in the 8 possible directions will make your ball deflect right, left continue straight or bounce back when it hits the intersection. You'll need to experiment with the controls the first game to get the hang of it.  To pause the game, press the SHIFT-LOCK key.

A game consists of three turns, and for each turn a timer counts down to zero. The timer counts down from 100 at level one, from 96 at level two and so on. At the higher levels, the ball also rolls faster. When you collect all the dots you advance to the next level. In level one, you earn one point for each dot you eat, in and end your turn. level two you earn two points, and so on. Clear a level, and you get a 1000 point bonus. Earn 10,000 points, and you win an extra turn. The turn ends when you run out of time or lose the ball.
 
OUT OF CONTROL
So far, so good. The hazards you find scattered along the paths, however, can quickly confound you! Spinners-the only permanent hazards-send the ball off in random directions. The other hazards turn off and on every few seconds. U-shaped magnets hold the ball until the hazards disappear. Round bumpers reverse the ball's direction. Diamond-shaped teleporters zap the ball to one of the spinners. Purple squares take the ball and end your turn.

games.name: Trax!
games.overview: You are the drive of a train which starts with 4 carriages. When you pick up a passenger from the trackside, you score as many points as there are carriages. You must avoid the Ghost Trian, which will attempt to crash into you! When all the passengers have been collected, pass through the tunnel from the Right for more. Every time you enter the tunnel you gain an extra carriage.

games.name: Traxxion
games.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter also published in Videogiochi Settimanale #01. Get the hell out of there" screamed his monitor. With a blinding CRAAASH the comet had struck TRAXXION. The system had gone berserk. Glowing like a dwarf star, the space platform is breaking up. Robocars speed in panic, beyond control of the system. With the screams of a tortured beast Traxxion begins to burn like a furnace. Time, the very gold dust of your life, is running out. You tear along the track and destroy everything in your path - everything in your sight.

games.name: Traz 2
games.overview:
In the rush to be the first one to use the level-editor to create an unofficial sequel to Traz, this one came in slightly behind, but with some really nice quality levels to play. Transformable Arcade Zone is a Breakout clone with multiple paddles, 64 levels and a built-in level construction set. Each level can have different set of paddles, sometimes one at the top and one at the bottom, sometimes one left one right, sometimes four stacked-up etc. This gives each level a distinctly new gameplay.

There are unbreakable blocks, monster generators (also unbreakable) and glass refractors that change the balls movement angle as it passes through.

After a level is cleared, the player must choose the next level by moving on a 8x8 grid of levels.

Published in Italy as Trap 2 in Super Game 2000 Nuova Serie n.15 (Aprile 1989) and also in Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - 100 games 90 (1990).

games.name: TRAZ II (Orion)
games.overview:
Transformable Arcade Zone II is a sequel to the original Breakout clone with multiple paddles, 64 levels and a built-in level construction set.

Each level can have different set of paddles, sometimes one at the top and one at the bottom, sometimes one left one right, sometimes four stacked-up etc. This gives each level a distinctly new gameplay.

There are unbreakable blocks, monster generators (also unbreakable) and glass refractors that change the balls movement angle as it passes through.

After a level is cleared, the player must choose the next level by moving on a 8x8 grid of levels. This is an all new set of levels.

versions.label: TRAZ II (1988)(Jon K. Menzies)[cr Orion][t Orion]
TRAZ II (1988)(Jon K. Menzies)[cr Orion][t +1 Orion]

games.name: TRAZ III
games.overview:
Transformable Arcade Zone III is a Breakout clone with multiple paddles, a ton of new levels. Each level can have different set of paddles, sometimes one at the top and one at the bottom, sometimes one left one right, sometimes four stacked-up etc. This gives each level a distinctly new gameplay.

There are unbreakable blocks, monster generators (also unbreakable) and glass refractors that change the balls movement angle as it passes through.

After a level is cleared, the player must choose the next level by moving on a 8x8 grid of levels

games.name: TRAZ Professional
games.overview: Traz Professional with an added Trainer.  This one just might melt your brain. Transformable Arcade Zone is a Breakout\Arkanoid clone with multiple paddles. Each level can have different set of paddles, sometimes one at the top and one at the bottom, sometimes one left one right, sometimes four stacked-up etc. This gives each level a distinctly new gameplay.

games.name: TRAZ: Transformable Arcade Zone
games.overview:
Transformable Arcade Zone is a Breakout clone with multiple paddles, 64 levels and a built-in level construction set.

Each level can have different set of paddles, sometimes one at the top and one at the bottom, sometimes one left one right, sometimes four stacked-up etc. This gives each level a distinctly new gameplay.

There are unbreakable blocks, monster generators (also unbreakable) and glass refractors that change the balls movement angle as it passes through.

After a level is cleared, the player must choose the next level by moving on a 8x8 grid of levels.

versions.label: TRAZ Transformable Arcade Zone (1988)(Cascade Games)[cr EDT]
TRAZ Transformable Arcade Zone (1988)(Cascade Games)[cr CMM]
TRAZ Transformable Arcade Zone (1988)(Cascade Games)[cr TSC][t TSC]

games.name: Tread Bear
games.overview:
Fred Bear has decided to have a cheese sandwich for his supper. Eating it has made Fred tired, so he falls asleep. He starts dreaming that he is driving through Toyland, which is occupied by fluffy snakes, wooden ducks, space men, toy trucks, and several other inhabitants. Unfortunately, touching any of these toys poses a danger to Fred as doing so causes damage to his car, and if the car inflicts enough damage, it breaks down and Fred is sent to heaven. Fortunately, Fred is equipped with a nuclear honey pot and some balls of honey, which can be thrown at the toys to put them out of commission.

The 1987 re-release by Alternative Software (Scare Bear) has different music.

games.name: Treasure Hunt
games.overview:
Treasure Hunt is a game based on a popular UK television series of the 1980's. In the program, contestants were given cryptic clues which led from one location to another. They had to decipher these clues and direct a real-life TV presenter and her camera crew to those locations in a helicopter.

The game follows the same pattern. It comes with a 60+ page book containing extracts from Ernest Benn's 'Blue Book' guides to England, Scotland and Wales, however the instructions do say that a large scale map would be useful too. The game consists of four hunts

    Greater London
    South Devon
    Anglesey
    The Fife Peninsular

versions.label: Treasure Hunt(P. Clement & R. van Hasselaar)

games.name: Treasure Island (Mastertronic)
games.overview:
The goal of Treasure Island is not too surprising: exploring an island and find the big treasure which is rumored to be found on it. Well, evading the deadly pirates is also a good idea. The game is loosely based on the novel and features Long John Silver.

The presentation is similar to any interactive fiction game with static graphics, but there are a few unusual features to be found. The first things noticeable are that the whole game is in real-time and the very limited parser, in fact all available commands are listed in the manual. The graphics update with every step (can be switched to walking or running) and can be zoomed in with the telescope the protagonist has in his possession.

Every action, including standing around, costs energy which has to be refilled by eating. Other features are a day/night-rhythm (time can be sped up by sleeping) and the possibility to leave behind flags for orientation. The game can be saved at any time.

games.name: Treasure Island (Mr. Micro)
games.overview:
Treasure Island is an arcade adventure based on the Robert Louis Stevenson's book. You play the role of Jim Hawkins who has to get to Treasure Island, defeat pirates and defeat Long John Silver.

Jim must get on to a ship and avoid the enemies before being whisked off to Treasure Island. On the island Jim must encounter and avoid various pirates. Scattered on the island are cutlasses which can be used to kill pirates blocking his path. Beware though, cutlasses are limited so Jim doesn't want to waste them on any old pirate. Get hit by a cutlass or touched by a pirate and you lose a live sending you back to the start of the screen.

Search the island, find Long John Silver and become rich beyond your wildest dreams.

The game is viewed from a side, top down view. The game doesn't scroll but flicks to the next screen as you explore this maze. Your score is shown as a percentage of the game completed.

games.name: Treasure Island (Pyramid Software)
games.overview:
Find treasure on a small island. X marks the spot! Become rich and famous. 

Very brief and simple game.

games.name: Treasure Island (Windham Classics)
games.overview:
Jim Hawkins is a young boy working on "Admiral Benbow", his parent's inn. One day a sea captain named Billy Bones takes a room at the inn and stays for several months. A blind man called Pew arrives and shows something to Billy that gives him a heart attack. Jim witnesses everything and runs to aid the captain, who tells him about his sea chest and his relationship with Captain Flint, a famous pirate. After he dies Jim grabs the key dangling from the corpse and opens the dead captain's chest to collect the last payment. He finds a packet inside, and decides to take it to two aristocratic acquaintances of his, Dr. Livesey and Squire John Trelawney. They discover a diary and a treasure map, and decide to travel to the island in search of the booty.

Treasure Island is a text adventure, an adaptation of the classic 1883 novel of the same name by Robert Louis Stevenson. Unlike the book, the game is written in a second-person perspective. Otherwise, it follows the original plot closely: the player assumes the role of Jim Hawkins, and has to perform the same actions as the character in the novel. This leads to a more claustrophobic design, as players without knowledge of the book have to guess what to do next. To help alleviate that problem, other characters act as some sort of built-in hint system. The player can ask them about anything and they will provide clues when these are available. The parser accepts most of Infocom's standard features like pronouns and chain commands.
.

games.name: Treasure Isle
games.overview:
Avast, me hearties! Shiver me timbers as well, but rub some soothing balm on them shortly afterwards, or things could get a little uncomfortable for me. Its a wonder how the pirates understood each other, actually. You could get into some pretty nasty scrapes on the high seas if you took one of those requests too seriously, some very nasty scrapes indeed.
One such scrape is the swashbuckling search for the Treasure Isle, and from that point the enormous stash of goodies that lie hidden on it. Will our intrepid adventurer reach his goal? Will untold wealth and riches follow. Only you (and the two word parser) will decide. 
Treasure Isle is a text adventure where you work out the best solutions to some foxing puzzles using only your will, cunning, lateral thought and keyboard skills can protect you!
Released as part of Commodore Format 1995/10 (Issue #61) and also Commodore Zone Issue #01.

games.name: Treasure of the Phoenix
games.overview: Fly through the massive tomb of King Tut on your powerful Eagle. The first chamber you must pass through contains many magical hazards including spears of death, bewitched saws, and horrendous boulders. The second chamber contains minions of the Devil. If you get past these and reach the door you will arrive in a different part of the tomb. The third chamber has never been seen by mortal eyes but it is rumored that a phoenix guards it at all times.

versions.label: Treasure of the Phoenix(Hitech Games Plus)[h ASS]

games.name: Treasure Quest
games.overview: A selectable answers text adventure published as a game of "The Big 100" collection. This program is an adventure, that is, it is a game set in an imaginary world that only the computer knows and you will try to get to know too. How? Just answer the questions your Commodore 64 asks you in kind. Let's take an example: at the beginning of the game, the program tells you that you are inside a cave and briefly describes the environment that surrounds you. It then gives you some indications regarding the direction to follow to recover the fabulous treasure: if you press the N key you will go North, S towards south and so on It is up to you, and above all your memory and imagination!

games.name: Treasure Raiders
games.overview:
Deep in the tomb of King Batutu is buried a treasure, untouched for centuries. Many have tried to find their way through the deep and dark corridors. No one has succeeded. Can you solve the maze? 

Each time the program starts, a new maze is drawn. You have ten seconds to view it before you start your trek. A timer starts when you begin. If you don't get through the maze in time, you'll starve, so be efficient in your moves. 
A help key will give you another quick look at the maze if you are stuck. Press H.
Released as part of "Commodore Pro-Pak" game pack.

games.name: Treasures of Ra
games.overview: Robotron meets Venture or something a bit like Shamus. Control Frank and help him safely through the tombs. Fire your swords at the hordes of monsters and find the treasures as you make your way through a maze-like dungeon seen from an overhead perspective.

games.name: Treble Champions
games.overview:
Treble Champions is a football management game. The player can manage a squad, train players, and try to gain the way to the top of the leagues and cups. There are four divisions of 20 teams each and 1,500 (fictional) players with individual attributes are included in the game and purchasable for the manager. Beside the squad skills and injuries, the finances have to be managed for further progress in the game.

All menus and handling are presented in text based menus, mouse control is not supported. The matches are presented in text messages and an overview statistic about possession and shots. During the game, no interaction or intervention is possible. Loading and saving options are present. There are three difficulty levels and the player can chose in which league he wants to start (starting in the premier league is possible).

versions.label: Treble Champions[cr DCS Federal Cracking Crew]
notes: Cracked by DCS Federal Cracking Crew

games.name: Tree Tutor for Tots
games.overview:
Tree Tutor for Tots is an educational math game for the Commodore 64.

You have the option to see the apples in the trees the whole time, or to only see the apples if you guess wrong.

Every time you answer correctly, a bird takes an apple from the tree and put it in a basket.

The game was developed as a type-in game by Janet Arnold and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/03 (Issue #09).

A version of the game was also released for the VIC-20 in the same magazine.

games.name: Trek Adventure
games.overview: Based on the original TV series. This one takes place aboard a familiar starship and is a must for Trekkies. The problem is a familiar one - the ship is in a "decaying orbit" (the Captain never could learn to park!) and the engines are out (you would think that in all those years, they would have learned to build some that didn't die once a week). Your options are to start the engine, save the ship, get off the ship, or die. Good luck.

games.name: Trenchfire
games.overview:
Released as part of COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/03 (Issue #09), 64'er Spielesammlung #5 as Ultrasonic it was released in Commodore Computer Club N°02. as Death Trench it was released in 75 Spill Datatronic, as Starfighter it was released in game of "The Big 100" collection, and as a part of the "Star Fighter" game pack.

A trench shooter based on the trench sections of the Star Wars arcade game.

games.name: Trener
games.overview: Trener is a soccer management game. The game allows you to choose one of the following options: Polish League, League of Nations, Europa League. In the first case the player can choose one of the eighteen teams from Extraklasa Polish League. In the second and third case the player has no choice - directs Poland and Legia Warsaw in leagues consisting of eighteen teams. The game offers the opportunity to carry out training, setting tactics, buying and selling players, determine the premium. During the match there is no animation. The match takes place in the form of text messages. Team manager may make changes in the composition, determine the tactics and level of aggression. After the match the game shows the results of the round and the current table. At the end of the season the club receives bonuses determined by the place in the table. The game has no sound.

games.name: Triacus
games.overview: An Italian side-scrolling shooter published in Commodore 64 Club #09. Sort of a Gyruss / Defender hybrid in which you have to shoot enough ships in order to get to the next level.

games.name: Triad (Adventure International)
games.overview:
Don't mistake this game and the 3D shooter from the following year from Livewire Software. 

The Commodore game of the same name is a combination Tic-Tac-Toe game and space shooter for 2 players.

The game starts as a Tic-Tac-Toe game, where nine separate icons are randomly assigned to each portion of the board. The include: an arrow, a green mask, a blue mask, an insect, a bat, a chess piece, a UFO, a spider, and a butterfly. When a player selects a location on the board, the game changes to an overhead shooter, where the player must defeat all enemies on the screen. If all enemies are defeated, the player gains the position. If the player is defeated by the enemies, then the position remains vacant. A player wins by obtaining three positions in a row.

games.name: TrianGO
games.overview: TrianGO is a variation of the board game Go that is played on a hexagon shaped board. The board is composed of 21 lines which cross to form triangles. The lines intersect to create 55 points where players can place their stones. The game is available for up to four players who take turns placing stones on the board. The aim is to capture the stones of the opponents by creating triangles. A triangle is created when three stones are positioned so that they can be connected with straight lines. All of the stones that are located within the triangle can then be captured if the player chooses to. When making a capture, both the player's own stones and those of the opponents are removed from the board. The player's own stones can be brought back into play while the opponents' are permanently out. To win the game the player has to become the last one still able to make a move (due to still having stones left).

versions.label: Triango (1988)(California Dreams Logical Design Works Inc.)[cr HTL]
versions.publisher: California Dreams Logical Design Works Inc.

games.name: Triaxos
games.overview:
A mind-probe has been sent to the maximum security prison Triaxos to retrieve information from a prisoner who is the only man who can activate the most powerful weapon in the galaxy. You have landed in the prison 10 minutes before the probe to find and get the man back to your ship within 30 minutes. You must search the prison blasting the robot guards and exploring each room.

Each room's floor is anti-gravity so can be stood upon to use other exits on any wall. To move to another wall you must use Face-Lifts, a disc in the middle of the room which allows you to transfer to another wall. Some exits are hidden but your map of each room shows the location of the exit. Dropping a DHE-IV Charge on the floor makes it appear. These are limited but more can be collected on the way. A Jet-Pack has to be found for the prisoner, a Defense Key to control the prisons defenses and a weapon to destroy the mind-probe. The Comms room is needed to be located to call in your ship and a cloning room is helpful to clone yourself but at the cost of energy.

Triaxos is a flick-screen arcade adventure with an isometric view. As well as the main playing area you can also see your energy bars, amount of charges, score and a timer ticking down to zero. There are also two maps, one of the whole prison and one of the room your in showing any hidden exits and objects on any wall.

games.name: Tric Trac
games.overview: Tric Trac is a dice based gambling game for 1-5 players. It was developed by Image Design and published by J & F Publishing in 1997.

games.name: Trick
games.overview: A good looking mine-sweeper code-breaking combo game.

games.name: Tricky (Markt & Technik)
games.overview: A logic brain-game.

games.name: Triget
games.overview: Triget is a Tetris/Columns like puzzle game developed by Ability and published by CP Verlag in the German based (although the game is in English) disk magazine Game On. It was published in Game On 1992/10.

games.name: Trigger Happy
games.overview:
You are Flight Commander McCoy and after saving the ship Thundercross you have been given a new mission from Space Control 25 to destroy 32 giant spacecraft high in the Stratosphere. In your Advanced Flight Capsule (AFC) you must fly alongside each ship and blast and destroy as much of the outside of the ship. This will include anything sticking out like blocks, shields and more importantly it's defenses especially as these will fire back at you. You do have a gun yourself, but you can only fire if you move the ship, and you can't move the ship while firing. You only have one attempt to destroy all 32 as you have one life, but you do have a shield which decreases if you hit an object or a bullet. Die past ship one, and you receive a password to start from that ship again.

Trigger Happy is a horizontal shoot-em-up viewed from the side, with the screen scrolling left to right constantly. As you are flying alongside the ships, then everything is behind you, so you shoot anything sticking out. A joystick is used to control your AFC.

games.name: Trigon
games.overview: Trigon is a 1987 Tron light cycles-type game for up to 3 players. Developed by Hansjörg Beck and published in 64'er Sonderheft 17.

games.name: Trilistron
games.overview: A 3D shooter from CRL/QuelleSoft and released in Germany. Your original mission was to construct a station with new and unknown technology on spiral arm 8 36. Unexpectedly, the sensors detected an unknown power field inside the planet TrilistronNhGenthullen, an unknown fading, blue-green planet. As you begin to investigate you are attacked almost immediately, without warning or explanation by a Trilistron space armada. The central observation computer ignores the indications that you should withdraw as the sector's strategic value is too important to be neglected. Only you and your spare ships remain to fend off the furious attacks. Suddenly calm, you know what you need to do, as paralyzing silence reigns in the control room you suit up, ignore the monotonous alert klaxon and prepare for battle.

games.name: Trilogy
games.overview:
Three Interactive Adventure Games, released independently for some systems but also in this compilation:

VENOM: You embark on a quest, travelling through the land in search of the evil plaguing the land.

KOBYASHI NARU: Three quests await you as you seek to join three items that belong to the Immortals.

SHARD OF INOVAR: As an apprentice, you must take over your master's role. But, you must first find the Shard of Inovar before the first rains hit to cast your spells....

games.name: Trilogy of Time
games.overview: A trilogy of text adventure games that contains "The Challenge of the Pirate King", "A Place of Safety" & "History's Twist".

versions.label: Trilogy of Time(Pinckney Benedict & Anthony Nalker)

games.name: Trio (CP Verlag)
games.overview:
Published in Magic Disk 64 1989/08. TRIO is a game where the focus is on the fight against the round ball. The main aim of this game is to use a stick to hold a ball within a playing field until a time limit has expired. During one of a total of four levels, as many points as possible must be scored, which can be achieved as follows:

If the ball touches one of the three animated points in the middle of the playing field, you get the number of points that appears at the top of the respective display. If there are three symbols of the same type, there is a mega bonus of three times the specified number of points.
With three jokers, the player is even credited 1000 bonus points. ATTENTION! Only three clubs are available to the player for each level;
Clubs are lost if the ball disappears or if an object is touched!

games.name: Trip to Atlantis
games.overview: Trip to Atlantis is a treasure hunting text adventure in which the player explores the lost city of Atlantis. In conventional fashion the player starts in a location with a sign that all treasures should be dropped there and the player can move from there to explore his surroundings, pick up items and solve simple puzzles. There are some hostile marine animals that have to be defeated as well as a maze. The game can also be saved into a single save-slot. Part of the Adventure Pak game pack.

games.name: Triple Tournament
games.overview: An exacting multi-genre test of Arcade action skills specially written for the Commodore 64. Including a shooting duel, an avoid-it action game, and a cross hairs shooter

games.name: Triplex
games.overview: Leave the pen and paper in the drawer, this Tic Tac Toe game is out of this world! Published in Game On 1992/03.

games.name: Triss
games.overview: Triss is a platform game, where the player must stop Hephyr from taking over the world. The main task requires recovering 20 magical stones of Thefrog, scattered around Hephyr mansion. Triss will meet many unfriendly creatures and unpleasant obstacles, but he will also several useful items. Eight items can be carried simultaneously. Triss is weaponless, therefore the only way to avoid enemies is proper use of jumping skill.

games.name: Tristan and Isolde
games.overview: An adventure game based on a famous Bavarian Legend. Our hero is Tristan, the honourable Knight. Tristan must save his beloved Isolde from the evil Wumper, bad Baron of Wummerstein. You must control Tristan on his gallant mission within Wumpers's sinister castle. Make sure you possess magic shoes - with these you can fly. Beware the evil Wumper, you must fight him at all costs!!

games.name: Triton
games.overview:
Triton is a 1-player vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by The Power Unit and published in both 64'er Disc 1990/01 and in 64'er 1999/07. A robust "Finger of Fire" is required for this shooter.  
 
In the year 2095 hostile aliens besiege the planet Triton in the Orion star system. A few resistance fighters have gathered in a remote area to develop a weapon against the invaders: the DX-11, a gigantic spaceship with ultra-modern equipment. The day of reckoning has finally come...
This is where you come in. Although you are neither involved in the resistance movement nor in the development of the fighter, you are given the "honorable" task of getting the potatoes out of the fire for the inhabitants of this planet. Well then, cheers! The aim of your mission is to destroy 100 ground stations in each level. You will be severely hampered by a few barriers that can neither be shot down nor flown over. Whole squadrons of alien spaceships scurry around between your feet and leave small guided mines as a nice souvenir. Your DX-11's protective shield can handle a total of eight of these mines.

games.name: Trivia: The Ultimate Quest
games.overview: Time to get your brain working and answer some trivia to get to the top of the triangle. Each question has a time limit to answer and you use F1, F3 and F5 to answer A, B or C. The triangle is made up of 21 squares. The bottom row has six squares worth five points. The second row has five worth 10 points and so on before you get to the last square worth 500 points. The aim is to fill all squares. You can get one question wrong or pass one question.

versions.label: Trivia The Ultimate Quest (1989)(Duck Soft)[cr DCS]

games.name: Trivial Fruit
games.overview: Trivial Fruit is a arcade quiz game where one person or up to four answer as many questions as they can to win the game. Before you play you can decide whether there is a timer to answer a question and you can choose the timer to be up to 995 seconds. You can decide as well how many players and if you want the short game or long game. On screen there is a 3x5 grid and when a question on a variety of subjects is asked each answer represents a fruit. Get the answer correct then the fruit appears in a set position in the grid. You then answer the next question. Get it wrong and if playing another person then it's their turn until they either win or get a question wrong. You can play by yourself but there is no score so you try to win in the least number of questions. The short game requires the winner to get just a line of three of the same fruit and the long game is to fill the whole grid with fruit.

games.name: Trivial Pursuit: The Computer Game: Commodore Genus Edition
games.overview: This is the earliest home computer incarnation of Horn Abbot International Ltd's classic board game, Trivial Pursuit. The game involves answering questions on one of six subject categories to gain moves, and answering questions on special squares to gain one of the six 'Wedges' you need to gain the right to take on the final winning question. Questions are aimed at British players - many entertainment questions are based on British TV, and sport questions relate to popular British sports. Two game modes are available: Single Player (which involves answering questions against the clock) and Multiplayer (where you can take on up to five human-controlled players). The computer reveals the answer, and you select 'yes' or 'no' to tell it whether you got it right. The question categories are exactly the same as the board game: Art & Literature, Science & Nature, Geography, History, Sports & Leisure, and Entertainment. However two different question styles are added to take advantage of computer technology - some questions relate to a picture or diagram and some relate to a piece of music. One additional feature not available in the board game is a statistical analysis of the number and type of questions answered correctly. This can be split into the performances of all the players, or the performance of an individual player within the six categories. It is especially useful at the end of the game, when choosing which category a player must answer to win the game.

games.name: Trojan Warrior
games.overview:
An evil sorcerer is jealous of a princess in the neighbouring kingdom as she has magic powers and she is doing good with them. Knowing he can use these powers for his own evil plans, the sorcerer kidnaps the princess and holds her in his kingdom. You are a mysterious horseman who has appeared on his flying horse to rescue the princess. Problem for you is that the sorcerer is forcing the princess to use her powers to heavily defend five regions which need flying across and destroying any baddies which try to stop you. You can fire against these baddies who come at you at waves and touching one or their bullets make you lose one of three lives. To help you there are power-ups which can be collected. Once you complete a region you have to travel through a tunnel at speed avoiding touching the walls.

Trojan Warrior is a scrolling shoot-em-up viewed from the side with the screen constantly scrolling from left to right which includes the tunnel sections as well. As well as the main playing area you can see your score and number of lives. A joystick is used to control your hero.

games.name: Troll
games.overview:
You are Humgruffin, a troll who has been transported to the Netherworld of Narc a land full of Goblins and crystals and ceilings to walk on. The only chance to escape is to reverse a spell that put him there. In each chamber is a crystal which needs to be collected and put in an amulet. You need to avoid the Goblins or being trapped by walls built by them. If you touch a Goblin then you start to turn to stone and transported elsewhere in Narc. To help you on your quest you can make holes appear in the ground for you to fall through into another part of Narc or make a Goblin disappear. You can use other objects as well and these include Pyramids (to jump up to the ceiling), Toadstools (summons a Dwarf to make holes in the floor) and Die (to make a random hole).

Troll is a 3D isometric game which shows both the floor and ceiling that can be walked on. The game is viewed at an elevated angle. The joystick or keyboard can be used and as well as the main playing area you can also see the icons you need to help you on your quest.

games.name: Troll Castle
games.overview: This game was originally published on the disk with issue 10 of Compute!'s Gazette magazine. It was part of the article 'Teaching your computer English'. Gather powerful magic items and defeat the troll.

games.name: Trollie Wallie
games.overview:
You are shopping at your local supermarket where you have to buy 40 items from your list. Problem is shopping here is dangerous with creatures roaming and obstacles in your way. You can lose one of your four lives by touching a creature, falling from a height or touching certain obstacles. Another problem you have is that you can only carry five items at a time, once you have five you must go back to the start to pay for them and store them. Switches also need to be find to make certain walls that are blocking your path disappear.

Trollie Wallie is a platform game that scrolls when you move in all directions with a small part of the supermarket shown on screen. As well as the main playing area, you can also see your score, lives, items on your person, total items and a bonus clock that counts down from 1000.

games.name: Trolls
games.overview:
This platform game features the small blue-haired cutesy creatures that were popular around the time (although surely not with most computer game buyers?). You play a Troll roaming the levels in the hope of rescuing as many baby trolls as possible - each level gives you a set minimum to retrieve before you can leave via the Pigstop.

Initially you have no weapons, and contact with the nasties costs you energy, but a Yo-Yo can be collected, which can be used not only to kill enemies, but also to smash blocks away and open up paths, and even (with practice) tied to a ledge to allow you to swing across a gap. 

Throughout the levels you will find the letters B,O,N,U,S and G released from bonus balloons or on killing an enemy - if at the end of a level your letters spell out Bonus or Bogus you go to the appropriate extra level. The former has a chance to gain extra lives, the latter must be escaped quickly to avoid losing a life.

games.name: Trolls and Tribulations
games.overview:
You play a troll set on an expedition into cavernous sewers to retrieve valuable relics. Guarding the treasure are monsters such as cretins, buzzards, skulls and spiders. The mazes are difficult to navigate and fraught with danger. One wrong move could send you plummeting to your death.

Trolls and Tribulations is a side scrolling platform game with some puzzle like mechanics due to it's unusual control scheme and movement. Most mazes begin with a barrage of cretins that must be dispatched in order to open the door to the main portion of the maze. Your character has a gun that is capable of turning the cretins into eggs. After shooting them, you must quickly shove the eggs into the sewer water as they will hatch back into cretins after a short time. Your gun has limited ammo but which can be replenished in the middle of the screen.

Once the cretins have been defeated, the doors to the main portion of the maze are accessible. Here is where you will find treasures to increase your point total. The mazes require careful navigation as some treasures are placed in dangerous locations. Keys need to be recovered to open further doors allowing you to proceed to the maze's exit. Other monsters are present in this part of the maze and cannot be destroyed by your weapon. Instead it will take careful timing and jumps to avoid being killed by them.

The game is divided into three levels which can be chosen at the start. Each level has multiple mazes to work your way through.

Joystick control is a little bit unusual. Aside from the normal left and right movement, pushing down shoots your weapon, pushing the button causes you to jump in the direction you are facing while pushing up does a vertical jump. When you move you will always move one complete step. This means you have to be careful when moving on small platforms as an extra tap on the joystick could send you off the edge. The structured movement gives the later parts of the maze a more puzzle-like feel than a straight action game.

games.name: Troll's Tale
games.overview: An evil troll has hidden all of the treasures of Mark, The Dwarf King. There are 15 treasures hidden throughout the land that you need to help locate. If you locate a treasure, but the troll is on the screen at the time, you will need to come back and find a way to make him leave. Troll's Tale is an adventure game which requires minimal typing, using the spacebar to select from several possible actions which are listed on the screen and pressing enter to perform the selected action.

games.name: Tron (Hebdogiciel)
games.overview: In the electronic ring of a powerful computer, fight against a killer robot, a cruel game of freesbee. One of the few TRON games that isn't a lightcycle\Worm\Snake game, created by Brun Hugues and published in both Hebdogiciel Hors Serie N°2, Hebdogiciel Software N°2.

games.name: Tron (System Editoriale)
games.overview:
Tron, a dueling worm\snake game for 1-2 simultaneous players was published in Commodore Club - software # 15 game compilation.  
 
Remember the fantastic Walt Disney movie, where the protagonist was projected into the fantastic dimension inside a computer? In this game you will be the hero of the terrible motor course that will see you engaged in exciting challenges both against the computer and against another player. There are six difficulty levels of play. Power! Take your joystick in hand and be ready to enter the Motodrome!

games.name: Tron (THS Software Studio)
games.overview: Lightcycle battle commence! You can't touch the hard-light remnant that flows behind your cycle or that of your competitors laser bike. Stay alive to win. Published in Italy as Laser Bikes in Hit Parade C64 n.46 (Giugno 1990) and in Special Program n.64 (aprile 1990).

games.name: Tronic
games.overview: A space themed German language text adventure. The ultimate graphic adventure. The earth in the year 2191 AD. After endless turmoil and wars, there has been more than twenty years of peace in the solar system. BTS, a massive, intelligent computer system, has taken complete power over humanity and truly controls everything. BTS, BIOTRONIC SCAN, was created by humans, to serve humanity. BTS takes care of everything about government business, about the weather and even about the well-being of every citizen. But then the catastrophe happens: BTS goes mad and gives humanity an ultimatum, BTS doesn't want to serve any longer longer, but rule and on the ruins of human civilization its own robot society will be built. You are the last TRONIC agent, graduate of a special school, and suitable for such orders. stop BTS before it enslaves humanity! The Time and BTS fight against you! TRONIC is one of the best German graphic adventures for the Commodore 64 on disk. A sentence parser that understands complex sentences, 45 hires pictures of very good quality, sprite control in all pictures, interactivity of main characters, background music and an absolutely variable gameplay guarantee hours of excitement. Nearly 8200 different solutions mean you won't get bored.

games.name: Tronic Cycle
games.overview: A worm\tron style game by William Westerman.

games.name: Tronic Force
games.overview:
A puzzle game developed by Twice Effects and published in Magic Disk 64 1995/03.

Instructions for TRONIC FORCE TRONIC FORCE is a special kind of logic game. The point is to recreate a pattern displayed by the computer with the help of stones. But stones can only be moved according to a given pattern, which makes things tricky.

To move rows vertically or horizontally, the arrow is brought to the edge of the playing field at the height of the row of stones to be moved and the fire button is pressed. The row is now shifted in the corresponding direction. So that it doesn't get too difficult, the stones can change their color by clicking on the desired stone with the arrow and the fire button. A level is over as soon as the stones on the large playing area of ​​the handicap in the lower right corner of the screen correspond.

games.name: Tronix the Wombat
games.overview: Tronix the Wombat is a Commando-inspired shmup made with Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit (a.k.a. SEUCK).

games.name: Troopa Truck
games.overview:
Troopa Truck is a version of the classic game Moon Patrol.

Here the player is driving a patrol wagon across the surface of Zon. There are obstacles and mines to lead over, ground based enemies in LasaSlamma tanks and aerial enemies in the form of missile firing HeliChargers. The aim of the game is to survive as long as possible to achieve a high score.

games.name: Trooze
games.overview: To win you have to put away all the stones on the playfield. If you click on one location then 4 stones to the right and 4 stones under that position will be inverted. That means all stones there get deleted and all stones deleted will now be set. There are extras that you can find, a heart increases your lives, a clock increases your time a bomb destroys 16 stones but it a trap. The arrow pushes you to the next level and a bag gives you a score bonus.

games.name: Tropical Fever
games.overview:
A 2D single full screen maze where a hunter had to catch back a bunch of animals escaped from a big cage located in the center of the screen (monkeys, lions, birds). The hunter had to use some bananas found along the maze path to attract monkeys and push them back into the cage.

A brave hunter finds himself in a jungle inhabited by wild animals that he must capture and take to the protective animal habitat. After you have captured the panther, you will need to cage it. You will then be able to move to another area of the jungle to catch the gorilla. To stop you have a chance: press the fire button on your joystick: the water will allow you to continue the hunt. Occasionally a bonus will appear on the screen, be quick and catch it! When you run out of water, you can refuel in a special container. You have three lives to complete your mission. When he finally manages to catch the gorilla, there will be other animals even more ferocious and difficult to hunt. If you manage to complete this difficult mission, you will take all the animals to the protective animal habitat. You will thus receive a prize for your skill and may even rate entry to the list of great previous scores!

Published in Italy as Caccia Grossa in Hit Parade C64 n.2 (febbraio 1986) and in Poke n.7 (novembre 1985).

games.name: Trouble at Bridgeton
games.overview: You've been left in charge of Bridgeton Asylum while the manager is away and you have messed up big time. You forgot to lock the main door and all the patients have gone out into the big bright world. You need to find them and round them all up before the manager returns and you get fired. Trouble at Bridgeton is a text adventure where text describes your location and any items of interest. You type in commands to control your player with the keyboard.

versions.label: Trouble at Bridgeton (1990)(Atlas Adventure Software)[cr TBT]

games.name: Trouble Bubble
games.overview:
One or two simultaneous players can tackle this marble madness-esque platformer. In Dreams anything can happen, even colored bubbles, normally calm and harmless turning in to sticky globes that wander around swallowing poor Andrea's toys. Out of breath and sweaty, Andrea wakes up and discovers that it was just a bad dream. But this bad dream gave him an idea for the next one, which begins on his next rest! Now he is dreaming of a whole world of new toys, which he has never been able to have and it is he who guides the bubbles towards th toys to wrap them and bring them to him. But there is another bubble that appears and tries to steal the toys. This game can be especially fun if played by two friends at the same time, which whips the game to a frenzied pace. There is a small red square on the route which will randomly rearrange things to be recovered, adding to the fun. 

Published as Bollicine in Italy in Top PlayGames n.22 (giugno 1987).

games.name: Trull
games.overview:
Trull is an action-arcade game, resembling the two popular games Snake and Pac-Man.
